en: At one time, the Blessed One dwelt within the wombs of the Vajra Ladies of the heart of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas,
together with unspeakably many bodhisattva mahāsattvas, as numerous as the atoms in the Mount Sumerus of all buddha-fields.
They were as follows:
and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Samayavajra;
and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Kāyavajra;
and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vāgvajra.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Cittavajra; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samādhivajra; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Japavajra.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Pṛthivīvajra;
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Abvajra;
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Tejovajra.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vāyuvajra,
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ākāśavajra,
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Rūpavajra.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Śabdavajra;
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Gandhavajra;
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Rasavajra.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Sparśavajra;
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Dharmadhātuvajra. Namely:
And by the Tathāgata named Akṣobhyavajra;
and by the Tathāgata named Vairocanavajra; and by the Tathāgata named Ratnaketuvajra.
And by the Tathāgata named Amitavajra; and by the Tathāgata named Amoghavajra. Namely:

Indeed, the entire realm of space was seen to be completely filled with all the Tathāgatas, like a sesame seed pod. Then, in order to please the Blessed One, the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, those Tathāgatas emanated their own forms as female forms and emerged from the body of the Blessed One Vairocana.
There, some remained in the form of Buddhalocanā, some in the form of Māmakī, some in the form of Pāṇḍaravāsinī, and some in the form of Samayatārā.

There, some remained in the form of the intrinsic nature of form, some in the form of the intrinsic nature of sound, some in the form of the intrinsic nature of smell, and some in the form of the intrinsic nature of touch.
Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, and the Tathāgata Vairocana [approached] the Tathāgata Bodhicittavajra...
He dwelt within the heart. Immediately upon his entering [samādhi], this entire realm of space became composed of the vajra of all Tathāgatas.

Then, as many sentient beings as there were residing throughout the entire realm of space, they all, through that empowerment of Vajrasattva, attained the bliss and mental well-being of all Tathāgatas.
Immediately upon being thus empowered, that very Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bodhicittavajra, appeared to all the Tathāgatas in a three-faced form.
"Excellent, excellent, O Blessed Ones! All Tathāgatas!
[they exclaimed. "Yet, since this causes doubt even for all the Tathāgatas, how much more so for other bodhisattvas?"
They questioned the Blessed One, the dispeller of the doubts of all Tathāgatas, the Lord of all Tathāgatas:

"Since the Blessed One does not venture to teach the secret of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas even within this assembly of all Tathāgatas so distinguished by such qualities, may the Blessed One therefore grant his empowerment through the words arising from the vajra-samaya of all Tathāgatas, for the sake of causing all Tathāgatas to experience bliss and mental well-being, and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the knowledge and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas."
"May he reveal it! [said] Vajradhṛk.

Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One—the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas—by means of the supreme states of union with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Akṣobhya, in the form of black, white, and red, sat upon the Body-Speech-Mind Vajra of all Tathāgatas within the Body-Speech-Mind Vajra of all Tathāgatas.
*Jinajik*. Then, in this...

Ratnadhṛk. Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Man of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, by means of the supreme states of union with the great mudrā of Ratnaketu, sat down to the right of the Vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, appearing in yellow, white, and black forms.
May there be light!

Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One— the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— sat upon the back of the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas in the form of red, white, and black, through the supreme states of union with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Lokeśvara, the Great Lord of Knowledge. He is the Holder of Wisdom (*prajñādhṛk*).

Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, by means of the supreme states of union with the Great Mudrā of Amoghavajra, in the form of green, white, and black, sat down to the north of the Vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas; he is Dveṣarati.

Then, as soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Vidyā-puruṣa of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, having assumed a form of glorious beauty, became Moharati within the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Then, as soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One— the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— having assumed a glorious form, sat down in the eastern corner as Īrṣyārati. Then [he sat down] in this [corner] as Rāgarati.
Then, as soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, having assumed a glorious form, sat down in the western corner.
Vajrarati.

Then, as soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One— the Knowledge-Person (vidyāpuruṣa) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— having assumed a glorious form, caused Yamāntakṛt to sit down in the northern corner.

Then, as soon as he had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Man of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, sat down at the eastern gate in the form of one who terrifies all Tathāgatas;
he is Prajñāntakṛt.

Then, as soon as he had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, sat at the southern gate in the form of the Vajra-Samaya-Terrorizer.

Then, as soon as he had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, sat at the western gate in the form of the Speech of all Tathāgatas— Vighnāntakṛt.

Then, as soon as he had emerged, that very Blessed One—the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas—sat at the northern gate in the form of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
He said: "Gentlemen, take up the mind in the form of the body, the body in the form of the mind, and the mind in the utterance of speech.

[One should realize] one's own mind as being free from all entities, devoid of the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, and abandoned by the grasped and the grasper; it is equal through the selflessness of phenomena, primordially unarisen, and of the nature of emptiness.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocanavajra:
"Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-dharmadhātu."
Teach the supreme mandala, which is peaceful, belonging to all Tathāgatas, the abode of all Tathāgatas, and the foremost selflessness of all phenomena. (1)
Complete with all the marks, yet devoid of all marks; the supreme assembly of speech, the foremost body of Samantabhadra. (2)
Arising from the supreme peaceful dharma, purifying the conduct of gnosis, the foremost speech of Samantabhadra—this is the most excellent maṇḍala of speech. (3)
The great mind of all sentient beings is pure and naturally stainless;
it is the supreme mind of Samantabhadra, the most excellent circle of sound.
Then Vajradhara is the Teacher, the one who belongs to the three worlds and the three realms;
he is the supreme, foremost Vajra of the three worlds, the instructor of the highest in the three worlds. || 5 ||
He speaks of the delightful mandala, the abode of all Tathāgatas;
the mind of all Tathāgatas is the mandala, having the form of a mandala.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of mind,
which resembles the vajra of mind— the maṇḍala of body, speech, and mind.
The wise one should trace the lines with a new, perfectly pure, well-measured, and beautiful thread, through the meditations on body, speech, and mind.
One should construct the supreme *cittamaṇḍala* measuring twelve cubits;
one should fashion it as square, with four doors and four corners. (9)
Within that, one should draw a circular wheel;
then, one should perform the placement of the mudrās according to the ritual procedure as seen in the scriptures.
In its center, one should draw a vajra with a five-pronged tip, possessing a brilliance like sapphire, emitting great flames, and terrifying even fear itself.
To the east is a great wheel adorned with vajra-flames;
to the south is a great jewel, dense and agitated by sparks.
To the west is the Great Lotus, with a radiance like that of a ruby;
to the north is the Great Sword, blazing and enveloped in a mass of flaming rays. (13)
In the eastern corner, one should draw the Eye, with a radiance equal to the midst of a cloud;
then, to the south, the Vajra born from the family of Māmakī.
To the west, one should draw a lotus with its stalk and fully blossomed face;
to the north, one should make an utpala flower, as beautiful as a dark blue cloud.
One should draw a mallet, brilliantly radiant with flames, at the eastern gate;
to the south, one should draw a staff, brilliantly radiant with vajra-flames and so forth. (16)
To the west, one should draw a lotus emitting the radiance of a flaming sword;
to the north, one should draw a vajra belonging to Vajrakuṇḍalī, the wielder of the vajra.
Having clearly realized the mandala as the most supreme of minds, one should diligently perform worship through the offerings of body, speech, and mind. (18)
Having obtained a sixteen-year-old woman who possesses beautiful radiance and has been adorned with perfumes and flowers, one should desire her in the midst of that [mandala].
And having embraced that Prajñā, who is Māmakī and girdled with virtues,
one should emanate the gentle state of a Buddha, adorned by the element of space.
One should offer feces, urine, semen, blood, and so forth to the deities;
in this way, the perfectly awakened ones and the high-minded bodhisattvas are satisfied. (21)

Thus ends the fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Secret Maṇḍala of Body, Speech, and Mind, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

—14— The Fifth Chapter Then the Blessed One, the Holder of the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, the King, the Foremost of All, the Lord of the World, spoke the characteristics of conduct for the sake of the supreme meaning of the Dharma and the foremost practice of the Dharma: 1. [He spoke] the characteristics of conduct for the sake of the supreme meaning of the Dharma and the foremost practice of the Dharma.
One should accomplish the supreme siddhi, which arises from the object free of conceptual construction and transcends the great turmoil of passion and hatred, in this unsurpassed vehicle.
Even those such as Caṇḍālas and bamboo-workers, who contemplate wealth for the purpose of killing, achieve success in this supreme vehicle, the unsurpassed Mahāyāna. (3)
Even those who have committed great evils, such as the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*), attain accomplishment in this Buddha-vehicle, the great ocean of the Mahāyāna. (4)
Those intent on reviling the teacher do not succeed in the practice;
nor do those beings who take life and who delight in false speech.
Those who always delight in the wealth of others, those who are constantly devoted to sensual pleasures,
and those whose practice consists of consuming excrement and urine— they indeed are fit for the spiritual accomplishment.
The practitioner who desires his mother, sister, and daughter shall attain vast accomplishment, the state of the supreme Dharma of the Mahāyāna. (7)
Desiring the Mother of the all-pervading Buddha, he is not defiled;
for that wise one who is free from conceptual construction, Buddhahood is accomplished. (8)
Then indeed, the great bodhisattvas headed by Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin were struck with wonder and filled with amazement.
"Why does the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, utter such ill-spoken words in the midst of the assembly-mandala of all Tathāgatas?
Then all those Tathāgatas, having heard these words of wonder from the great bodhisattvas headed by Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin, spoke thus to those bodhisattvas: "Enough! (15) #
Sons of good family, do not speak thus!

This is that pure nature of reality (dharmatā) of the Buddhas who possess knowledge of the essence; born from the meaning of the essential Dharma, this is the stage of the conduct of awakening (bodhicaryā). 9.
Then, indeed, the bodhisattvas—equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields—became afraid, terrified, and fainted.
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, seeing all those bodhisattvas fainting, spoke thus to the Blessed Lord of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas:
"Blessed One, please rouse these great bodhisattvas!"

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajra, entered the meditative absorption named the Non-dual Vajra Equal to Space. As soon as the Blessed One, the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, had entered it, those Bodhisattvas were touched by his light and remained seated in their respective places.
Then all those Tathāgatas, having attained a state of wonder and amazement, overflowing with joy, uttered this sound of Dharma:
"Aho! Dharma! Aho! Dharma! Aho! Source of the meaning of Dharma!
O Vajrarāja, pure in Dharma and in the sense of selflessness, homage, homage! (10)
Purified in body, speech, and mind, abiding in the equality of space, changeless and without appearance—homage, homage to the Vajra Body! 11.
Homage again and again to the supreme mind of the Tathāgatas, which moves along the paths of the three times, which has become the great space of the elements, and whose nature is space. 12.
Born from the body of space, the activator of speech that is space, the supreme dharma of the mind that is space—homage be to you, the stage of conduct! 13.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, the Chapter on the Supreme Universal Conduct, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the King of Great Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

—16— The Sixth Chapter Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhyavajra entered the meditative absorption named the "Secret Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas" and uttered this mantra for the empowerment of the mind:
*Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-mind of all Tathāgatas.*
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocanavajra, having entered the samādhi called Virajapadavajra, uttered this mantra for the empowerment of the body:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra body of all the Tathāgatas.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyurvajra, having entered the meditative absorption named "The Non-dual Vajra of the Equality of All Tathāgatas," uttered this mantra for the empowerment of speech:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the speech-vajra of all Tathāgatas.

One should accomplish the pure state of the Tathāgata, the triple vajra, which is the manifestation of the [enlightened] state, by means of these excellent mantras characterized by their defining marks. (1)
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketuvajra, entered the samādhi called Jñānapradīpavajra and uttered this mantra of enchantment:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra that impassions all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhivajra, having entered the meditative absorption named Amoghavajra, uttered this mantra of worship:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the worship of all Tathāgatas.
One should always worship the Buddhas according to the rules with the five strands of sensual pleasure;
through the worship of the five offerings, one shall swiftly attain Buddhahood. (2)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara, the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One, Vajradhara, the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed this secret mantra of all Tathāgatas:
*Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.*
Impelled by body, speech, and mind through the contemplation of the mantra,
one should accomplish the most excellent siddhi, which is dear because it satisfies the mind.
Through the selflessness of mental composure and the dissolution of speech and body,
they accomplish the union that is the abode of equality with space.
Through the contemplation of body, speech, and mind, no intrinsic nature is perceived;
by means of the application of the mantra-form, there is cultivation within the bodhicitta.
Having briefly reflected upon this characteristic of body, speech, and mind,
one should cultivate the meditative absorption (samādhi) fashioned by mantra, joined with the ritual procedure.
Then the glorious Vajradhara, accompanied by all the Tathāgatas, the omniscient one who is foremost among all Buddhas, spoke this supreme meditation: (7)
One should meditate on a moon mandala situated in the midst of the space element;
having visualized the form of the Buddha, one should commence the subtle yoga.

One should contemplate a mustard seed at the tip of the nose; within that mustard seed, one should meditate upon the entire world of moving and non-moving beings—this beautiful secret, fashioned by wisdom, which bestows knowledge.
One should meditate on a sun-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having visualized the form of the Buddha, one should place the mantra-syllable above it. (10)
One should meditate on the maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
one should visualize the union of Locanā’s form within the vajra-lotus.
One should meditate on a jewel maṇḍala situated in the center of the space element;
with diligence, one should visualize the primordial yoga upon it. (12)
One should meditate on a lotus maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
one should meditate on Rāgavajrin, perfectly joined with the form of a lotus. 13.
One should visualize a circle of light rays situated in the midst of the space-element;
one should then emit the peaceful state of the Buddha and, in particular, his retinue.
One should diligently visualize at the tip of the nose a five-pronged trident, specifically shaped like the petal of a blue lotus and measuring the size of a barley grain. 15.
One intent on awakening should clearly visualize this eight-petaled lotus, with its filaments, the size of a chickpea seed, at the tip of the nose. 16.
One should specifically perform meditative cultivation (*bhāvanā*) there upon the wheels (*cakra*) and other [mudrās];
thus one shall attain the delightful state of awakening, which is the abode of the qualities of mantra-attainment. || 17 ||
Therein, one should briefly emanate that which is established in the awakening of the Buddhas;
one should cause to issue forth the word of Dharma, characterized by body, speech, and mind. (18)
Then the glorious Vajradhara, the teacher of the meaning of all reality, who has arisen from the foremost of all practices, spoke this supreme secret. (19)
For six months, the wise one, endowed with form, sound, and taste, should practice meditation;
having performed the great worship of the secret reality, he should contemplate it.
One who desires the fruit of accomplishment should perform the function of consuming feces and urine;
thus, the unsurpassed reality—the stainless *bodhicitta*—is accomplished. (21)
For the purpose of performing such acts as the consumption of meat, one should prepare "great flesh" (mahāmāṃsa);
thus the secret of body, speech, and mind is accomplished among all attainments.
One should eat the meat of elephants, the meat of horses, and likewise the excellent meat of dogs for the purpose of sustenance; one should not consume any other [meat]. 23.
He becomes beloved by the Buddhas and by the wise Bodhisattvas; indeed, through this very yoga, he shall swiftly attain Buddhahood. (24)
In this world, he shall become a lord of the realm of desire, a performer of supreme deeds;
he will be radiant, powerful, preeminent, beautiful, and pleasing to behold.
Impelled by this very vision, one should honor him in this world;
for this is the secret of all Buddhas, the supreme awakening, the reality of the mantra-secret characterized by body, speech, and mind. (26)

Thus ends the sixth chapter, the Chapter on the Empowerment of Body, Speech, and Mind, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
—20— Chapter Seven. Then the Blessed One, the Lord of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed this chapter on the supreme awakening of the mantra practice of the Great Compendium:
"By enjoying all objects of desire as one wishes, through this very yoga, one shall indeed swiftly attain Buddhahood. (1)
While enjoying all objects of desire as one pleases,
one should worship with the supreme limbs through the yoga of one's own presiding deity.
One who practices with severe and difficult observances does not achieve success;
however, by enjoying all objects of desire while practicing, one achieves success quickly.
One who subsists on alms should not perform recitation, nor should he be devoted to begging;
one whose limbs are not impaired by the recitation of mantras may enjoy all objects of desire.
Having attained stability of body, speech, and mind, one attains enlightenment;
otherwise, one certainly undergoes untimely death and is cooked in hell.
Buddhas and bodhisattvas who practice the supreme conduct of mantra have attained the most excellent Dharma-seat through the enjoyment of all desired objects.
One should always serve the five who move at will, the masters seeking knowledge;
one should satisfy the Bodhisattvas and cause them to rejoice through the hero of passion. 7.
Having understood form in its threefold way, one who is devoted to worship should perform worship;
he is thus the Blessed One, the wise Buddha, the Lord Vairocana. (8)
Having understood sound to be of three kinds, one should offer it to the deities.
Such is the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Lord who is a mine of the jewels of the Buddhas. (9)
Having discerned the three kinds of fragrance, one should offer them to the Buddha and the others;
he is indeed the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Lord who upholds the dharma of passion. 10.
Having understood the threefold flavor, one should offer it to the deities. He is indeed the Blessed One, the Buddha Bimba, who possesses the unfailing vajra. 11.
Having recognized the threefold touch, one should offer it to one's own family;
thus that Blessed One, the Vajrī, becomes one who attains the form of Akṣobhya.
One should always apply forms, sounds, tastes, and so forth to the mind;
this is the compendium of the secret essence of all Buddhas. 13.
The practitioner of mantras should always meditate upon the deity through touch, sound, and so forth;
or else, he should meditate there by means of the discernment of the various divisions of the *kula*. 14.
The cultivation of mindfulness through the application of the recollection of the Buddha;
the cultivation of the recollection of the vajras of body, speech, and mind through cultivation. || 15 ||

Through the yoga of recollecting the family, one should cultivate the recollection of the wrathful deity; by means of the yoga of recollecting the commitment (samaya), one who meditates thus shall attain awakening. 16.
Having approached each such woman who possesses that power and is radiant with beauty,
one should perform worship in secret while maintaining mindfulness of the state of the foundational locus (adhiṣṭhāna-pada).
One should meditate upon Locanā, who is the great radiance of the Tathāgata;
through the union of the two organs, one shall attain the siddhi of a Buddha. || 18 ||
One should conceptualize the syllables HŪṂ, OṂ, and PAṂ, and meditate upon a vajra-lotus pervaded by five-colored rays of light. || 19 ||
One desiring awakening should meditate on that delightful [deity] as having blazing rays like a vajra;
one who desires awakening should meditate on the applications such as the recollection of the Buddhas.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the Buddha performed?
One should visualize the form of the Buddha through the union of the two organs;
the wise one should radiate clouds of Buddhas from the openings of the pores of the skin. (21)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the Dharma performed?
By means of the union of the two organs, one should visualize Vajradharma;
the wise one should emanate clouds of Dharma from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin. (22)
—22—In that regard, how is the meditation on the recollection of the Vajra performed?
By means of the union of the two organs, one should visualize Vajrasattva;
the wise one should emanate clouds of vajras from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin. —23—
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the family (kulānusmṛti) performed?
One should visualize the form of the Buddha through the union of the two organs;
the wise one should emanate clouds of the family from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin. (24)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of wrath performed?
One should visualize the Lord of Wrath through the union of the two organs;
the wise one should emanate clouds of wrath from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin. (25)

In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the pledge (samayānusmṛti) performed? Through the application of the two organs, one's own vajra joined with the lotus, one should worship the Buddhas and Vajrasattvas with the drops of one's own semen. || 26 ||

In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the mandala performed? Through the union of the two organs, the wise yogi should always emit from the [central] mandala those [emanations] that have the form of mandalas. (27)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of mindfulness of the body [performed]?
"May my own body also become like that of all the Buddhas, filled with the five aggregates, by virtue of its nature as the Buddha-body. (28)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of speech?
"May my speech also become like that of Vajradharma, possessing the perfection of the definitive expression of words, so that I may be equal to a Holder of the Dharma. (29)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the mind?
"Whatever is the mind of the wise Guhyakendra Samantabhadra, may my mind also be such as that, equal to the Vajra-holder. (30)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of sentient beings [practiced]?
"Whatever mind belongs to all sentient beings, characterized by body, speech, and mind, such a mind is also mine—pervading like space. (31)
—23—In that regard, what is the cultivation of the recollection of the body, speech, and mind of the form of all mantras?
"Whatever is the body of the Mantra-Vajra, and the visualization of his body through speech—may my own mind likewise become like that of the Holder of the Mantra. (32)

In that regard, what is the cultivation of the recollection of the pledge (samayānusmṛti)? One who desires the fruit according to the rule should honor the array of the Tathāgatas by means of the ritual of the syllables of the pledge; thus one will most certainly attain accomplishment. || 33 ||
Likewise, what is the cultivation of the recollection of the samaya of the perfection of wisdom?
All things are luminous by nature, unarisen, and free from outflows;
there is no awakening, no realization, no end, and no origination. (34)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of non-arising?
Everything is luminous by nature, signless, and beyond syllables;
it is neither dual nor non-dual, peaceful, like space, and utterly pure. (35)
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the worship of the Hatred Family performed?
Having obtained a twelve-year-old woman of steady mind, one should worship her with one's own semen according to the specific distinctions of the family yoga. (36)
By this, one shall attain in this very life the body of the Tathāgata, the mind of the Vajra-holder, and the speech of the supreme Dharma-holder.

Those who are considered of inferior birth, as well as others, attain accomplishment through his recitation and by meditating on the indivisibility of the three vajras, once the body, speech, and mind have been perfected. (38)
Thus ends the seventh chapter, the Chapter on Mantra Practice, in the *Śrī Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the Ultimate Secret of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
Chapter Eight: Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, requested the Blessed One Mahāvajradhara—the Lord of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas—with this King of Praises:
“O Vajrasattva, you who purify the practice of the space-like Great Vehicle!”
O Samantabhadra, supreme among victors, teach the foremost of offerings. || 1 ||
O Vajra of passion, hatred, and delusion, who reveals the Vajrayāna; O Supreme One, like the expanse of space, whose voice is worship, O Abode of the Victors! || 2 ||
O Buddha, the guide to the path of liberation, who establishes the way of the three vehicles, whose nature is pure through auspiciousness, O Supreme among Men, please accept this offering. (3)
O Bodhicitta, wide-eyed one, turner of the wheel of Dharma, pure in body, speech, and mind—homage be to you, Vajrayāna! 4.
Then King Vajradhara, the great syllable of all space, the purpose of all consecrations, the Lord of all, who holds the vajra-jewel; || 5 ||
He proclaims the supreme worship of the Tathāgatas, which is established in the indivisibility of the three vajras,
the auspiciousness of body, speech, and mind, born from the source of the Victors.
Having obtained a large-eyed maiden adorned with beauty and youth,
one should fashion her secret parts as twenty-five finger-breadths wide.
In a clean, secluded spot on the earth, which is a peaceful and auspicious abode for the Son of the Jina,
one should constantly perform the smearing with pure water and other substances for the sake of worshipping the Jina.
The knower of the ritual should place [the mantras] between the breasts and up to the middle of the topknot, as well as within the space between the eyebrows;
he should perform the placement of the five families of the Sons of the Jinas upon the navel, the hips, and the private parts.
One should meditate on the ocean of gnosis situated in the center of the space-element;
then, one should again meditate upon oneself within the moon, located in the heart. (10)
If he who holds the peaceful vajra should desire [to perform the rite], he should effect the withdrawal;
[he should visualize] a stūpa composed of the four jewels, adorned with blazing rays of light. (11)
Having dispatched the woman as the ocean of gnosis, the wise one should contemplate her abode;
he should radiate clouds of offerings from the pores of his own skin.
Having understood the five kinds of lotus and the blue water-lily, the wise one,
having prepared the three types of birth-garlands, should offer them to the deities.
Having meditated upon the flower of the *karṇikāra*, as well as the *mallikā*, the *yūthikā*,
and the flower of the *karavīra*, one should perform the worship.
One who is skilled in constant meditative concentration should visualize a wheel-mandala with an extent of a hundred yojanas and should perform the rites for the [five] families. 15.
The wise one should visualize a lotus, a vajra, a sword, and an utpala, extending for ten million yojanas, square-shaped, and most beautiful. (16)
The wise one should meditate upon a caitya made of the four jewels, transparent and naturally stainless, as a fly-whisk for the purpose of worshipping the Kulas.
One should begin with the pure Yādavī using the five strands of sensual pleasure;
desiring awakening, one should constantly worship her with jewels, garments, and other offerings. 18.
One should always satisfy the deity with the five supreme offerings;
[one should offer] a maiden who brings forth jewels, most excellent, and adorned with various gems and ornaments. (19)
For the sake of attaining accomplishment for all the Buddhas, the fervent practitioners, being wise, should offer this [mandala], having made it complete with the seven jewels. (20)
Desiring the accomplishment of the ocean of generosity, the wise one should offer [this] every day, having taken up the Arcipatimudrā in the midst of the Buddha-maṇḍala. (21)
One should bestow the union of touch with a mind of passion toward the Buddhas; one should meditate upon the mandala of the Buddhas situated in the midst of the space-element. 22.
Those who worship an image of the Tathāgata according to the prescribed rites quickly obtain a fortunate woman of beautiful countenance and great splendor. (23)
Having meditated upon the station of the empowerment, one should perform the worship of reality;
the wide-eyed one of firm intellect should consume the secret semen. (24)
This is the worship of the body, speech, and mind of all mantras;
it is declared to be the secret that brings about the accomplishment of mantra for those who possess the vajra of gnosis. (25)
Thus ends the eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Mind-Samaya, in the *Śrī Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the Ultimate Secret of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.

Chapter Nine: Then Vajradhara, the King, the Great Immutable One of all space, the Foremost in all consecrations and conduct, the All-Knowing Supreme Lord, [spoke]: 1. [Verse omitted as per instructions]
One should proclaim the union of body, speech, and mind, the mandala of the indivisible three vajras,
which is supremely delightful and the secret of those possessing the wisdom of the Buddhas.
One should visualize the mandala of the Buddhas situated in the midst of the space-element;
having visualized Akṣobhyavajra, one should visualize a vajra in one's hand. (3)
Having meditated upon the majesty of the Buddha, which is strewn with a dense mass of sparks and filled with five-colored rays, one should pulverize it there with a vajra.
One should meditate upon the supreme dhyāna, which brings about the accomplishment of the mind, wherein the union of body, speech, and mind is pulverized by the eight vajras. (5)
By means of this secret vajra, one should destroy all sentient beings.
Furthermore, those who are the sons of the Victors in his vajra buddha-field should be known as the union of the Hatred family, which is the exaltation of all families. (6)
Then King Vajradhara, the accomplisher of wisdom and liberation,
pure by nature and stainless, is the one who sets in motion the conduct of awakening.
He speaks the commitment and the reality that accomplishes the awakening of the Buddhas;
one should meditate on the maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element. (8)
Having visualized Vairocana, one should visualize all the Buddhas;
by means of the application of all jewels, one should fashion the vajra-image. || 9 ||
One should visualize the seizing of all substances with the triple vajra;
they become like wish-fulfilling jewels, filled with an ocean of wealth.
The preeminent sages become the legitimate sons of all Buddhas;
those born of all families should know that the reality is equal to the family of delusion. 11.
Then King Vajradhara, the accomplisher of passion and delusion, pure and without support in the secret [realm], proclaims the mandala: || 12 ||
One should visualize a lotus mandala situated in the midst of the space-element;
having manifested Amitābha, one should fill everything with Buddhas.
One should visualize the union with the form of a woman for all [practitioners] therein;
by means of the yoga of the four commitments, this is the supreme Vajra Way. 14.
By means of the application of the two organs, one should enjoy them all;
this is the meditation on the indivisibility of the three bodies of all the Buddhas.
The practitioner of mantras should indeed cultivate the union of the passion family. || 15 ||
Then King Vajradhara, the accomplisher of the meaning of the vajra-mantras, who has realized selflessness through the arising of primordial wisdom, spoke these words: (16)
One should visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
having manifested Vajrāmogha, one should then visualize all the Buddhas.
One should contemplate all forms through the vajra-word of false speech;
one should deceive all the Jinas as well as all the abodes of the Jinas. 18.
This is the utterly pure space of speech of all Buddhas;
it is declared to be the secret of those with wisdom and intelligence, which brings about the accomplishment of mantra. (19)
The family of the summoning of the pledge should be impelled according to its true meaning.
Then King Vajradhara, the leader of the Vajra of Accomplishment—the indestructible vajra of the three vajras—spoke these words: (20)
One should meditate on the pledge-maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
having manifested Ratnaketu, one should emanate this through all forms.
"By practicing even through harsh speech and the like, one shall attain gnosis.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Array of Vajras of All Tathāgatas. 22.
Then indeed, those great bodhisattvas, headed by Sarvatathāgatasamayavajraketu, being struck with wonder and filled with amazement, uttered this sound of the vajra of speech:

"Why does the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, speak these vajra-words of marvelous meaning within this assembly of all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattvas— words concerning things that transcend the three realms and transcend all world-systems?"

Then the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus to those great Bodhisattvas—headed by Sarvatathāgatasamayavajraketu—who were as numerous as the atoms in the Sumerus of ineffable, ineffable Buddha-fields:
"Do not, O sons of noble family, give rise to this notion of inferiority or this notion of loathsomeness. For what reason? Because..."

Noble sons, the practice of passion is indeed the practice of a bodhisattva; it is the supreme practice. Noble sons, it is just as space is all-pervasive, and all phenomena are pervasive within space.
They do not abide in the desire realm, they do not abide in the form realm, they do not abide in the formless realm, and they do not abide in the four great elements.
In this very way, noble sons, all phenomena are to be understood.
Having realized this purpose and having discerned the inclinations of all sentient beings, all Tathāgatas teach the Dharma.
In the same way, noble sons, those samayas of the Tathāgatas are to be understood through the etymological analysis of the term "space-element."

Sons of good family, it is just as, for example, when smoke appears and fire is produced in dependence upon a fire-drill, a fire-board, and the exertion of a man’s hands; yet that fire does not abide in the fire-drill, nor in the fire-board, nor in the exertion of the man’s hands. In the same way, sons of good family, all the vajra-samayas of the Tathāgatas are to be understood.
"By means of going, coming, and so forth.
Then all those bodhisattvas, having attained wonder and amazement, their eyes wide with astonishment, uttered this cry:
"Regarding these most marvelous phenomena, which are like space..."
In those states that are non-conceptual and pure, it is conventional reality that is proclaimed. || 23 ||

Thus ends the ninth chapter, the Chapter on the Commitment (*samaya*) Concerning the Ultimate Non-dual Reality, from the *Śrī Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittarahasyātirahasya Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras.

Chapter Ten: Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again assembled in a great gathering, paid homage to the Blessed Lord of All Tathāgatas, the Tathāgata who is the secret of body, speech, and mind—the Great Commitment Vajra Reality of Perfect Awakening—and spoke as follows:
Speak, O Blessed One, the reality that is the compendium of the essence of mantra,
known as the secret of body, speech, and mind, the supreme system for great accomplishment.
Thus [ends the first section]. || 1 ||
Then King Vajradhara, the Lord who brings an end to all afflictions, with radiant complexion and wide eyes, spoke these words: || 2 ||
The cultivation of the body, speech, and mind of the vajras of body, speech, and mind is non-conceptual, without objective support, and equal; it does not abide anywhere. (3)
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Svabhāvaśuddha, entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Pāramitā-Mantra System and addressed all those Tathāgatas as follows:
"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, headed by Akṣobhya, display the drama of all purposeful activities through many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of vidyās.
Throughout all world-systems, extending to the limits of the world-systems in the ten directions, they sport, delight, and are surrounded by the five qualities of sensual pleasure."
And they do not look upon one who is devoted to the practice of mantra. For what reason?
Because, "Ah! this person has indeed perfected the reality of the dharma within the method of the Tathāgata’s mantra practice."

Therein, for the sake of surveying those great beings, he uttered this collection of mantras from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind— this supreme secret of the Great Mystery, called the "Exhortation of the Heart of Mantras," which is the focal point of the samaya of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, the focal point of the samaya of the body, speech, and mind of all Vajradharas, and the focal point of the samaya of the body, speech, and mind of all Dharma-holders: Oṃ Āḥ Svāhā.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the Buddhas together with their spiritual sons trembled and fell into a swoon, recollecting Vajrasattva.
-31- Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed this samaya:
"One should visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
one should imagine the syllable HŪṂ situated there in the middle as one's own form. || 5 ||
One should visualize [the deity] blazing intensely with great vajra-rays, radiating light;
one should contemplate that by this, the body, speech, and mind of the Buddhas have been seized. 6.
At that very moment, he becomes the holder of the vajra of body, speech, and mind—Vajrasattva, the great king, the foremost of all, the supreme lord. || 7 ||
The procedure for accomplishing one's own maṇḍala by means of one's own mantra shall be as follows;
this is the essence of all Buddhas, the *Vajrasamuccaya*. (8)
Having meditated on the person of one’s own mantra in its formal aspect at the four locations,
one should visualize it through the yoga of the three-faced form in three colors.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Khavajrasamaya.
In this regard, this is the supreme secret of the vajra:
the visualization of the mandalas as subtle, situated within the center of the heart.
One should contemplate the supreme syllable, the ultimate state, situated in its center.
The knower of yoga should always meditate upon the great five-pronged vajra;
he should contemplate the three vajras according to their various divisions, such as the vajra-hook and so forth. 11.
One should strike the heart with that [mudrā] and impel the deity and so forth;
this is the preparation of the Buddha-image for all Vajras. || 12 ||
By means of the two hands [forming] a wheel and a lotus, one should visualize a vajra and a hook;
this is declared to be the "urging" at the heart, arising from the drama. (13)
One should perform this supreme Vajra method for up to seven days;
thus, the secret of body, speech, and mind is accomplished for those possessing the Vajra of Gnosis. 14.
The givers of boons look upon them with minds both fearful and terrified,
yet they grant vast accomplishment that is dear to the heart and brings satisfaction.
If Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the supreme practitioners of mantra-conduct,
should transgress [the rules] out of delusion, that shall be the end of their life.
Then King Vajradhara, the supreme instructor of the three worlds, uttered this proclamation concerning the supreme vajra-peak of the three worlds: || 17 ||
As many as there are mantra-beings filled with the three vajra-knowledges, through the application of the two organs, all conceptualization of phenomena [is purified]. 18.
This is the mantra-samaya practice of all the Buddhas.
Among those who have entered into the Sovereign of All, there is the meditation on the union of the vajra.
One should behold her as red with red eyes; this is the samaya-maṇḍala. (19)
Then King Vajradhara, the son of all the Tathāgatas, the foremost of Buddhas regarding all consecrations, spoke these words: || 20 ||
In all world-systems, however many women are known to exist, one should enjoy them all through the application of Mahāmudrā. (21)
"Therein one should emanate the state of Buddhahood of incalculable tens of millions of Vajra-holders.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Samaya.
"By this, one shall attain enlightenment, which is like the sky of the three vajras."
He shall become the foremost Vajrasattva, an ocean of Victors of the Bodhicitta.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Exhortation of the Heart of All Tathāgatas," in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Chapter Eleven. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind, entered the meditative absorption named "Vajra Supreme Person" and proclaimed this Chapter on the Vajra Supreme Person of the Mantras of All Tathāgatas:
"The visualization of the Great Mudrās is performed by means of the supreme mantras of the three vajra syllables."
This should be performed with the vajra of knowledge, which brings about the realization of all enlightenment. || 1 ||
The syllable Oṃ is the heart of gnosis, which brings about the vajra body;
the syllable Āḥ is awakening and selflessness, which brings about the vajra speech. || 2 ||
"The syllable *hūṃ* brings about the body, speech, and mind, which are as indestructible as the three vajras.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Mantra-Purusha of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
"Situated in the center of the space-vajra, one should contemplate the mandala that encompasses all vajras."
One should meditate there on the syllable *bhruṃ*, which radiates forth clouds of vajras.
In this regard, here is the heart of the wisdom-vajra:
Bhṛūṃ.
One should visualize the syllable Oṃ situated in the center of the vajra-maṇḍala; one should contemplate the syllable Āḥ situated in the center of the translucent maṇḍala. || 4 ||

The visualization of the syllable HŪṂ situated in the center of the Dharma-maṇḍala; having meditated on the syllable BHRŪṂ as the abode, one performs the meditation on the arising of the three vajras. (5)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Secret Samaya:
"The heart-essence of the Buddhas of the three times, which delights body, speech, and mind;
the syllable Oṃ, the supreme body of the Buddha; and likewise the syllable Āḥ, the path of speech. (6)
The syllable HŪṂ is the flood of the wisdom of the mind; this is the supreme method for awakening.
This is that which accomplishes the awakening of all Buddhas. (7)
That which is emanated by the wisdom-vajra, arising as the cause and fruit of Buddhahood—these indeed are the Buddha-persons, renowned as mantra and vidyā. (8)
Through the pledges of accomplishment and so forth, and through the meditations on the indivisibility of the three vajras,
this is the samādhi named "The Cause for the Empowerment of the Knowledge-Vajra of the Reality-Pledge of All Tathāgatas."
One should undertake this yoga in secluded and delightful places;
body, speech, and mind will be perfected within a single fortnight, without a doubt. (9)
One should visualize the supreme, translucent maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having brought forth one’s own mantra-samaya, one should place the syllable Oṃ in the heart. 10.
Through the supreme meditations on Vairocana, one produces great clouds of five-colored rays;
by this, the body of the Buddha becomes the ocean of Vajravairocana.
One attains accomplishment in a mere fortnight, with a radiance equal to the body of a Buddha;
by practicing the five knowledges, one may remain for three vajra-aeons. 12.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Secret of the Body-Vajra.
The samādhi called the Array of Light-Rays from the Body of All Tathāgatas.
One should contemplate the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having brought it forth, one should place the syllable ĀḤ—the person of one’s own mantra—upon the path of speech.
Having accomplished the five-colored great vajra through the supreme meditations on Lokeśvara, one should bring forth the elaboration of the samaya-knowledge speech-samaya.
Established in the speech of the Dharma, one becomes equal to the Vajra of Dharma;
by serving those possessed of the five knowledges, one may remain for three vajra-aeons. 15.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Secret Vajra of Speech.
The samādhi named "Arising from the Vajra-Samaya of the Speech of All Tathāgatas."
One should contemplate the supreme vajra-maṇḍala situated in the center of the sky-vajra;
having produced the person of one's own mantra, the syllable HŪṂ, which is established in the mind. || 16 ||
One should indeed visualize the reality of the great samaya as having five colors;
this abode of all Vajra-Jinas must be performed by means of the Wisdom-Vajra. 17.
The Teacher, equal to the Vajra-mind, shall become an ocean of the qualities of primordial wisdom;
by serving those possessed of the five wisdoms, he shall remain for three eons of the Vajras. (18)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Secret Vajra-Mind.
The samādhi called the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
Having concentrated upon the great vajra in the center of the mandala of gnosis, one becomes equal to the gnosis of the space-vajra through the syllable *khaṃ* in all activities. || 19 ||
Khaṃ.
Being worshipped again and again by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
he may remain for the duration of three kalpas, yet even by the Buddhas he is not seen.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Khavajrasamaya.
This is the samādhi called the Garland of Arrays Arising from the Inner Blazing of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind.
Having meditated upon one’s own mantra-person within the center of the vajra-maṇḍala...
Having placed what is called the Vajra of the syllable HŪṂ in the heart, one should perform the visualization of its rays of light. || 21 ||

He becomes the very self of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the enjoyment-body (saṃbhogakāya) born of the samaya, possessing the vajras of body, speech, and mind, and established upon the ten stages. || 22 ||
The samādhi called the Moon-Vajra of the Bodhisattva’s Knowledge-Samaya.

Having meditated on the syllable *thlīṃ*, blazing with radiant light, situated in the center of the sphere of space, one becomes equal to the Vajra-body by means of the Vajra-body of supreme nectar. || 23 ||
thlīṃ || ||
The samādhi called the Abode of the Array of the Vajra-Samaya of Space.
Through the supreme samayas of the superknowledges of the Buddhas, one becomes equal to those possessing the five superknowledges.
This is the supreme means for accomplishing the superknowledges of all the Buddhas. || 24 ||
One should contemplate the supreme vajra-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having manifested Vajrasattva, one should manifest him in the form of primordial wisdom. || 25 ||
Oṃ.
"By means of meditation on the samaya of the three vajras, one becomes equal to Akṣobhya of the three vajras," said the Blessed One, Akṣobhyavajra:
"With a body equal to Akṣobhya, always upholding the supreme speech and mind, he is worshipped in all the world-systems by the wielder of the Akṣobhya-vajra. (26)
The samādhi called the Vajra of the Perfect Awakening of the Body of the Akṣobhya-samaya.
One should contemplate the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the element of space;
having manifested the Space-Vajra, one should manifest the form of the syllable TRĀM. || 27 ||
Trāṃ.
"By means of the meditation on the three-vajra samaya, one shall become equal to the Banner of the Three Vajras," said the Blessed One, Ratnaketuvajra:
"Through the vajra of body, speech, and mind, one possesses a radiance equal to Ratnaketu;
he becomes the bringer of the vajra-knowledge of awakening and selflessness. (28)
The samādhi named Ratnaketu-samayasambhogavajra.
One should contemplate the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having manifested Lokeśvara, one should visualize the syllable *dharmauṃ*. (29)
Oṃ.
"By means of the meditation on the three vajra-samayas, one becomes equal to the Three Vajras of Immeasurable Life," so said the Blessed One Amitavajra:
"Through the vajra of body, speech, and mind, one possesses a radiance equal to Amitāyus;
he shall become the source of the emergence of the Mahāyāna path for all sentient beings. (30)
The samādhi named "The Glory of the Power of Immeasurable Vajra."
One should contemplate the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having manifested the vajra-lotus, one should manifest the pledge-syllable Oṃ.
"By means of the meditation on the samaya of the three vajras, one becomes equal to the unfailing three vajras," thus spoke the Blessed One, Amoghavajra:
"Through the vajra of body, speech, and mind, one possesses a radiance equal to the unfailing vajra;
he becomes a glorious ocean of gnosis, the source of the welfare of all sentient beings. (32)
The samādhi named "Arising from the Supreme Knowledge of the Rays of the Unfailing Pledge."
One should contemplate the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having manifested Vairocana-vajra, one should manifest the three syllables Oṃ.
Oṃ oṃ oṃ.
"By means of meditation on the samaya of the three vajras, one becomes equal to Vairocana-vajra," so said the Blessed One, Vairocana-vajra:
"Through the vajra of body, speech, and mind, one possesses a radiance equal to Vairocana;
he becomes the awakening of gnosis, the achiever of the indivisibility of the three bodies. (34)
The samādhi called the Vajra of Perfect Awakening regarding the objects of body, speech, and mind.
This collection of meditations should be practiced in secluded mountains, by rivers and waterfalls, and even in cremation grounds and similar places. (35)

Having meditated upon Akṣobhyajñānavajra and the others in the center of the space-vajra, one should perform the cultivation of the supreme Buddhas in their respective places through the application of the five supernormal knowledges (pañcābhijñā). 36.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Vajra who has mastered the vajra-samaya:
"The great five-pronged vajra, adorned with five flames, through application in five places, one becomes equal to the five superknowledges. (37)
One should meditate on one’s own mantra as a wheel, dense with a mass of sparks;
through the application of the five vajras, one becomes equal to those possessing the five superknowledges. (38)
One should contemplate [the syllable] situated in the center of the space-vajra, possessing a radiance equal to the blazing of the Buddhas;
having meditated thus, through the entry of the Buddhas, one becomes equal to the abode of the Buddhas. || 39 ||
One should place Vairocana within the body, situated in the center of the Buddha-maṇḍala;
having meditated on the syllable Oṃ at the heart, there is the cultivation of the mantra-consciousness.
When that which has entered the vajra of cessation arises in his mind, he becomes the glorious wish-fulfilling gem, the supreme accomplisher of all Buddhas. || 41 ||
One should visualize Vajrākṣobhya situated in the center of the Buddha-maṇḍala;
having meditated on the syllable HŪṂ at the heart, one should place it within the mental drop (cittabindu). || 42 ||
One should visualize Amitābha situated in the center of the Buddha-maṇḍala;
having meditated on the syllable ĀḤ in the heart, one should place the mind-drop (cittabindu) there. 43.
This is the supreme pinnacle of commitments, the indivisible meditation of the three vajras;
it is the gnosis of the commitment of cessation, which brings about the accomplishment of Buddhahood.
One should meditate on the clear maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having visualized the syllable Oṃ within body, speech, and mind, one remains for an eon. (45)
One should meditate on the Dharma-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra-realm;
having contemplated the syllable ĀḤ within body, speech, and mind, one remains for an eon. 46.
One should meditate on the vajra-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra-realm;
having contemplated the syllable HŪṂ within body, speech, and mind, he remains for an eon. (47)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Samaya of the Three Vajra Wisdoms:
"Whoever should recite or even contemplate this extensive Yoga of the Vajra-holder of Body, Speech, and Mind, he too shall become a Vajradhara. (48)

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Supreme Vidyā-Puruṣa, the Vajra of the Reality of the Mantra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas," in the *Śrī-Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Chapter Twelve Then the Teacher Vajradhara, the Creator, the supreme practitioner of gnosis, whose speech is the reality of the three-vajra commitments, uttered this vajra-word: "This drama is manifested within phenomena that are pure by nature, which have arisen as equal to the space-element and possess a non-conceptual intrinsic being. (1)
In great forest regions adorned with fruits, flowers, and the like,
or on a solitary mountain, one should accomplish the collection of all siddhis.
ṃaṃ ||
Through the cultivation of Mañjuvajra within the vajras of body, speech, and mind, there is an emanation throughout body, speech, and mind; one becomes equal to Mañjuvajra. (3)
Adorned with all ornaments, the perfected being illuminates an area extending for a hundred yojanas with his blazing vajra-light.
The gods, beginning with Brahmā and Rudra, never perceive it at any time.
The samādhi called "Mañjuśrī-vajrāgra-samaya-antardhānakarī" (The Concealment by the Supreme Vajra-Samaya of Mañjuśrī). || 5 ||
Having prepared the five pledges of feces and urine, which arise from the indivisibility of the three vajras,
and having combined them with the three metals, one should place them in the mouth and meditate.
One should manifest therein the mind of all Buddhas, which is indivisible;
at that very moment, he shall become equal in radiance to Mañjuvajra. || 7 ||
Having empowered the wheel, which is brilliantly radiant with sparks, by means of one's own mantra, and having meditated upon it as the abode of all Buddhas, one shall become equal to a Buddha. (8)
As many atoms as there are in thirty-six Sumerus,
so many attendants he shall have, all equal to Vajradhara.
(9) -40- This is the samādhi called Akrasamaya.
Having meditated upon the great vajra in the center of the mandala with one's own mantra, one becomes equal to the Mind-Vajra, the abode of all vajras. 10.
As many atoms as there are in thirty-six Sumeru mountains,
so many women shall there be, who are abodes of virtue.
He becomes the great vajra of the three realms, honored by Rudra. || 11 ||
The samādhi called "the equality of the vajra."
Having meditated upon a great eight-petaled lotus with his own mantra-vajra, which is the abode of all phenomena, he becomes equal to the inconceivable Dharma. 12.
The pure-souled one establishes as many atoms as there are in thirty-six Sumerus within the supreme maṇḍala for the worship of the Buddha. (13)
The samādhi called "equality with the lotus."
He shall remain for the duration of three eons, serving those possessed of the five knowledges,
and attending upon the triple secret of all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
One with large eyes should meditate on one's own mantra as a sword with a radiance equal to five-colored rays; by grasping it in the hand, one becomes a Vajra-Vidyādhara. 15.
Worthy of great worship in the three realms, saluted by the lords of the Daityas and the Brahmas, that best of men becomes a Brahmā, a great hero of the triple-thousandfold world system. (16)
Whatever the holder of the vajras of body, speech, and mind desires with his mind, he bestows such a siddhi as is manifested by the mind-vajra. || 17 ||
The samādhi named Sarvakhaṅgottama (Supreme of All Swords).
Having meditated on a pill of the syllable Oṃ the size of a chickpea husk,
one should visualize the form of one's own deity within it and contemplate it in the mouth.
At that very moment, he would become equal in radiance to a Bodhisattva.
Resembling the rising sun, he possessed a radiance equal to that of refined gold.
Having meditated on a pill consisting of the syllable ĀḤ, the size of a chickpea husk,
one should contemplate the form of one’s own deity within it and visualize it in the mouth.
At that very moment, he becomes equal in radiance to the thought of awakening (bodhicitta);
he resembles the rising sun and possesses a luster like that of Jāmbūnada gold. || 21 ||
Having meditated on a pill made of the syllable *hūṃ* the size of a chickpea husk,
one should visualize the form of one's own deity within it and contemplate it as being in the mouth.
At that very moment, he becomes equal in radiance to the vajra-body;
he resembles the rising sun and possesses a luster like that of Jāmbūnada gold. || 23 ||
One should visualize Vairocana situated in the center of the pure space-element;
having visualized a wheel in one's hand, one becomes a holder of the wheel-vidyā.
Having meditated upon the great wheel family, this supreme practice of the wheel should be performed by the Wisdom-Vajra through the yoga of the supreme body of the wheel. || 25 ||
One should visualize Jñānākṣobhya situated in the center of the space-element vajra;
having manifested a vajra in his hand, he becomes a Vajra-vidyādhara. || 26 ||
Having meditated upon the great Vajra family, this supreme Vajra sādhana should be performed by means of the Wisdom-Vajra through the yoga of the supreme Vajra-body. || 27 ||
One should visualize a jewel-vajra situated in the center of a jewel-maṇḍala;
having visualized the jewel in one's hand, one becomes a Vidyādhara of Jewels. || 28 ||
Having meditated upon the Great Jewel Family, this supreme jewel sādhana should be performed by the Wisdom-Vajra through the yoga of the supreme body of jewels. (29)
One should visualize Amitābha situated in the center of a lotus within the element of space;
having visualized a lotus in his hand, one becomes a Padmavidyādhara. || 30 ||
Having meditated upon the Mahāpadma family, this supreme practice of the Lotus [family] should be performed by the Wisdom-Vajra through the application of the Dharmakāya. || 31 ||
One should visualize oneself standing in the center of the samaya of the space-element as Amoghasiddhi;
having visualized a sword in one's hand, one becomes a Vidyādhara of the Sword. || 32 ||
Having meditated upon the Great Samaya Family, this supreme practice of the samaya should be performed by the Wisdom-Vajra through the yoga of the body-samaya.

The trident, the wisdom-goad, and so forth are to be accomplished through the differentiation of the vajra; they are mastered by means of his meditation and the practices of body, speech, and mind. (34)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāsamayasiddhivajra:
"At a crossroads, or at a solitary tree, or at a single linga, or in a temple of Śiva, the practitioner should constantly accomplish the summoning of Vajra, especially with distinction. (35)

Having meditated upon the person of the mantra of the three yogas, the Vajra-holder of the three yogas, who is the hook of the body, speech, and mind of the Buddhas whose intellects are wisdom, [one should proceed]. (36)
Standing at the center of the wind mandala, one should perform the supreme summoning of the Buddhas;
having drawn them in with the vajra from the samaya-born [beings] of the ten directions, one should enjoy them. || 37 ||
The summoning of the vajra of the samaya of the element of space.

Having meditated upon Vairocana as the great wheel and the hook that is the abode of the Victors, one should perform the supreme summoning of the pledge-beings (samaya) by means of the vajra, lotus, and other symbols. || 38 ||
The summoning of the pledges of the three realms.
One should visualize the form of the Buddha endowed with the excellence of all aspects;
and one should visualize the body, speech, and mind in the hand, as well as the hook and other implements. (39)
By this very yoga, he indeed becomes a performer of others' tasks;
he should meditate upon the vajra-body endowed with the excellence of all aspects. (40)
By meditating through the application of the tongue-vajra, one becomes equal to the Speech-Vajra.
Having performed the supreme worship of the three secrets' pledge, one should bring about manifestation. || 41 ||

"This is the essence of all accomplishments, the Guhyasamuccaya," thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Secret Samaya. By means of the foremost samaya of human flesh, one should accomplish the supreme Triple Vajra.
By means of the ritual application of feces and urine, one becomes a powerful lord of the Vidyādharas. || 42 ||
By means of the flesh of the elephant-convention, one shall attain the five superknowledges;
by means of the flesh of the horse-convention, one shall become a lord of invisibility.
The accomplishment of all siddhis is achieved through the samaya of dog-flesh;
the supreme vajra-attraction is achieved through the foremost samaya of cow-flesh. 44.
If no meat is available, one should meditate upon and conceptualize a sentient being;
by this vajra-yoga, one is empowered by all the Buddhas. 45.
Endowed with the excellence of all aspects, possessing the vajras of body, speech, and mind; the pledge of gnosis in his heart, and bearing the supreme vajra upon his crown. (46)
This supreme method of the samaya is the gratification of all Buddhas;
it must be performed by means of the foremost samaya, for it is the highest bringer of all accomplishments. || 47 ||
The samādhi named "Vajra-Consumption of the Wisdom of All Samayas."
Having meditated upon the Vajra-holder HŪṂ at the tip of the tongue-samaya-vajra, one shall attain the state of Vajrasattva through the application of the five nectars. || 48 ||
This is the commitment of the syllables ĀḤ and OṂ, the supreme Vajra method.
Indeed, by means of this yoga, one becomes equal to Vajrasattva. (49)
The samādhi called Samayavajrāmṛtamālinī.
For the sake of accomplishing the samaya of the three vajras, one becomes a holder of the vajra of the three bodies;
for all the Buddhas of the ten directions, one becomes an ocean of wish-fulfilling jewels.
The one whose nature is vajra illuminates the world-realm in every direction;
at the conclusion of the accomplishment of the wheel-samaya, he becomes equal to the body of a Buddha. 51.
Having attained accomplishment, he shall wander everywhere, as far as all the sands of the Ganges;
in all the foremost samayas, he shall become a lord of the Vidyādharas.
Through the power of the Body-Vajra, he is the foremost in the accomplishment of all samayas;
among all forms of invisibility, he is the sole illuminator of a thousandfold world-system.
He takes away all accomplishments and enjoys the maiden born from the foremost of gods. 53.
With the vajra-eye, one beholds Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in the abode of the three vajras, as clearly as if they were a single object in one's own hand.
Whatever sounds are proclaimed by fields equal to the whirlpools of the Gaṅgā,
he hears them from all sides as if situated within his own ears, through the power of his supernormal knowledge.
He knows the characteristics of the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings—those which are like the sands of the Ganges—as they arise like a drama within what is called "mind. (56)
For eons equal to the sands of the Ganges, he would remember the occurrence of his existence in saṃsāra and the times of his former lives as if they were only three days.

For as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, the wielder of the firm and supreme vajra should emanate activities equal in number to the sands of the Ganges, adorned by clouds of Buddhas and other [deities]. (58)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Knower of the Samaya:
"The vajra-eye, the vajra-ear, the vajra-mind, Vajrapāṇi, and vajra-miraculous power—
through the complete accomplishment of the purpose of the Buddha’s superknowledges, one becomes equal to the body of a Buddha."
Surrounded by retinues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, he whose body and speech are vajra-like shall traverse the world-systems in every direction. (59)
The union of the time of service, arising from the near-attainment;
the time of the purpose of attainment, and the fourth, the great attainment.
Having understood this through the piercing of the vajra, one should then accomplish the ritual activities.
One should cultivate the union of service and meditative absorption, which is the unsurpassed liberation of awakening. 61.
At the culmination of the accomplishment of the *upasādhana*, there is the investigation of the vajra-abodes;
in the *sādhana*, the impelling is declared to be the meditation on the Lord of Mantras.
During the times of the great accomplishment, having meditated on the Lord as the crown ornament upon the image of one's own Mantra-Vajrin, one attains the state of a Knowledge-Vajrin.
One should never, under any circumstances or at any time, act without the nectar of service and knowledge;
for this indeed accomplishes the purpose of all mantras among all mantras. (64)
In great forest regions, in vast solitudes,
and in mountain caves and thickets, accomplishment (siddhi) is always attained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāsādhanavajra:
"Then, with the fourfold vajra, service (sevā) should be performed by those of firm vows;
meditating with the mantra of the three-vajra body, one attains accomplishment. (66)
Through the practice of the four junctions, the wise one, having meditated upon the vajra of the knowledge of the syllable Oṃ in the five locations, shall enter Saṃvara.
Having generated the Vajra-samaya for seven days, a fortnight, a month, or even a year, accomplishment is swiftly attained.
I have explained this in detail according to the distinctions of the days; within a fortnight, success is said to arise from those born of the foremost secrets.
In this regard, the following concerns the commitment (*samvara*) of the subsidiary means (*upasādhana*):
"May the glorious one, who bears the Buddha-body and is cultivated through the indivisibility of the three vajras, bestow upon me today the state of empowerment as the Vajra Body. (70)
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are meditated upon as inseparable from the three vajras, grant me today the state of empowerment characterized by the [three] bodies. (71)
In this regard, the following concerns the subject of the *sādhana-saṃvara*.
The glorious Dharma, whose path is speech and who is cultivated as the indivisibility of the three vajras—may he today grant me the state of empowerment for the Vajra of Speech. (72)
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who have cultivated the indivisibility of the three vajras,
grant him the state of empowerment arising from the path of speech.
In this regard, here is the section concerning the commitment (*samvara*) of the Great Accomplishment (*mahāsādhana*):
"May the glorious holders of the mind-vajra, who are meditated upon as the indivisibility of the three vajras, grant me today the state of empowerment, O Vajra-minds! (74)
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are meditated upon as the indivisible three vajras and who arise from the mind, grant me the state of empowerment this very day. (75)
Whether it be the Buddha, Vajradharma, or even Vajrasattva—if one who is deluded by nature should transgress [this command], they would shatter; of this there is no doubt. (76)

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, the teaching on the preeminent practice of the pledge (*samayasādhanā*), in the *Śrī-guhyasamāja*, the great king of secret tantras, the most secret of secrets concerning the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Chapter Thirteen: Then the Blessed Ones, the Tathāgatas who move at the pinnacle of the wisdom-vajra, and the wise Bodhisattvas who have arisen for the benefit of all sentient beings, prostrated before the Great Teacher, the Sage, the Vajra-holder for the sake of beings, the knower of the reality of the offering-pledge, and uttered this vajra-sound:
Oh, the divine method of the Buddha! Oh, the supreme method of awakening!
Oh, the peaceful method of the Dharma! Oh, the firm method of mantra! 1.
When phenomena have not arisen and possess no excellence of intrinsic nature, the arising of knowledge regarding those non-conceptual phenomena is proclaimed. (2)
Speak, O Blessed One, the delightful compendium of all dharmas,
the vajra-recitation of great gnosis, the mandala inseparable from the three bodies.
The wisdoms of the Buddhas are attained through the meditations on the indivisibility of the three vajras;
by reciting with the application of the vajra, one is empowered by all the Buddhas. || 4 ||
Having proclaimed the mantra recitation characterized by body, speech, and mind for all the families and all mantras, he then explained the vajra-recitation.
And the Buddhas, arisen throughout the three times, possessors of the vajras of body, speech, and mind,
have attained incomparable gnosis through the cultivation of vajra mantras.
Thus [ends the sixth].
Then the Teacher Vajradhara, born from the wisdom of the space-vajra,
the creator, the progenitor, the most excellent and supreme among the best, proclaimed the vajra-recitation.
In the recitations of the meaning of all mantras, this is the characteristic of the indivisibility of the three vajras;
this placement [of syllables], ending with the vajra in the three divisions, is called the "three vajras. (8)
And so it is said:
"A threefold vibration should be performed in the presence of body, speech, and mind;
by means of this vajra-recitation, one becomes equal to the Vajra-mind. (9)
Having meditated upon the body, speech, and mind of the Buddhas, the arrangement of worship should be performed by means of the Wisdom-Vajra; this brings about enlightenment. (10)
Alternatively, one should perform the radiation individually according to the three divisions;
one should cause the selflessness of body, speech, and mind to radiate forth by means of the gnosis-mind. (11)
Uttering [the mantra], one should emanate the vajra; at the conclusion, one should indicate the withdrawal.
This is the [method] of all Buddhas whose eyes are opened by primordial wisdom. 12.
The realization of enlightenment through the body-vajra, which is the investigation of existence and non-existence, is proclaimed as the Buddha-body; that is called "body-recitation. (13)
The awakening to the convention of speech, the investigation of words and non-words—this is declared to be the Vajra of Speech; it is called the recitation of speech.

The awakening to the commitment of the mind (*cittasamayasambodhi*) and the investigation of the vajra of stability—this is declared to be the "vajra-mind," and it is called the mental recitation (*cittajāpa*). || 15 ||
Then, through the recitation that follows along, which is beautiful and devoid of intrinsic nature, the investigation into the Buddhas of the three times is called the "jewel-recitation. (16)
The pervasive radiation of clouds of bodies from all directions throughout the Buddha-fields for the sake of the vajra-activity of going and returning is called the "unfailing recitation. (17)
One hears the syllables and words of the mantra within the mandala shaken by one's own vajras;
that is called the wrathful recitation through the wisdom of the wrathful samaya. (18)

Having established beings—who have become distraught for the sake of sensual desires and who seek neither protection nor welfare—upon the ground of delusion, it is known as the "Recitation of Delusion. (19)
Speech arising from the Vajra of Passion, which is established in body, speech, and mind—by establishing sentient beings in the state of passion, it is known as the "recitation born of passion. (20)
The mind arising from the vajra of hatred is established in body, speech, and mind;
having established sentient beings in the abode of hatred, that is called the recitation of hatred. (21)
The reality of the three-vajra commitment is the central Samayavajrin;
that very state is called the neuter recitation of all vajras. || 22 ||
All the Vajra-lords, who contemplate the reality of the meaning of passion, bring about the awakening born of passion, which seeks the welfare of all sentient beings. || 23 ||
The great vidyās, Locanā and the others, who are eternally devoted to the purpose of desire, are accomplished through the enjoyment of desires when they are practiced according to one's wish. (24)
The Vidyārājas, the Vajrins, who have arisen from the pledge of delusion, are perfected in the state of the neuter and bestow supreme accomplishment. (25)
Born from the abode of anger and hatred, they are constantly intent on killing; when served by those desiring wealth, they achieve success for the purpose of slaying. (26)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Being’s Vow:
"One should meditate on the wheel located in the center of the heart for those possessing the vajra of gnosis;
the meditation on the meaning of the wheel-mantra is situated within the midst of a translucent mandala. (27)
One should meditate on the vajra situated in the center of the heart of the Wisdom-Vajra-holder;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the vajra-mantra, located in the center of the vajra-maṇḍala. (28)
One who possesses jewel-like wisdom should meditate on the jewel situated in the center of the heart;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the jewel-mantra, located in the middle of the jewel-maṇḍala. (29)
The knower of the lotus should meditate on a lotus situated in the center of the heart;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the lotus mantra, located in the center of the Dharma-maṇḍala. (30)
One who possesses the knowledge of the sword should meditate on a sword situated in the center of the heart;
