this is the meditation on the meaning of the sword-mantra, located within the midst of the pledge-maṇḍala.
One should establish all the Buddhas on all sides of the maṇḍala;
by radiating them through the differentiation of five rays of light, one attains enlightenment.
The vibration of all mantras is proclaimed to be twofold by way of division;
through the division of the three vajra-bodies, there occurs the radiation and reabsorption. (33)
By worshipping the body with its own nature, the mind with the nature of the mind, and speech with the nature of speech, one shall obtain the merit of worship. || 34 ||
Through the great maṇḍala wheel, one meditates on the five vajras; having visualized the Lord in the center as one's own form, the possessor of the three kāyas of vajra. (35)
Having visualized the fourfold mandalas of one’s own Mantra-vajra according to the four colors, one should meditate on the meaning of the mantra within the heart. (36)
The fourfold vajra performs the activity of the one who possesses the meditation-vajra;
for this is the supreme, eternal secret of all mantras. 37.

In rites for pacification, one should take the form of Locanā; in rites for enrichment, the form of Padmavajrī; in rites for subjugation, the state of Vairocana; and in rites of sorcery, the form of Vajrakrodha.
This is the secret of all mantras, arising from the three bodies; it is manifested by the Wisdom-Vajra and characterized by the drama of ritual action. (39)
This rite of incitement should be performed against beings who speak with lack of devotion, those who revile the Teacher or the Vajrī, and other wicked individuals as well. (40)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahājñānacakravajra.
One should visualize all those dwelling in the three realms within the body of the Buddha;
having performed the opening and closing of the joined palms, one then carries out the accomplishment of activity.
One should visualize Vajrasattva, who is situated in the center of the element-space, possessing a five-pronged vajra and four faces, endowed with the excellence of all aspects. 42.
One should visualize the Buddha-wheel, which has arisen from the samaya of the three times;
this Buddha-wheel of great power is to be performed with the right hand. 43.
Having gathered together the sentient beings born in the ten directions through the differentiation of the Buddha-body,
one should cause them to enter into one's own body by means of the yoga of the mass.
Furthermore, the vibration is the activity of the Buddhas who possess the vajra of gnosis;
having meditated upon them as wrathful, agitated by rage, and terrifying with their formidable and fierce appearance. (45)
With the tips of their hands grasping various weapons and intent on the foremost purpose of killing, they destroy the greatly wicked ones—even Vajrasattva himself. (46)
The Buddhas, who grant the boon of the three bodies within the maṇḍala that is the abode of the three vajras, bestow accomplishment; a person of deluded nature dies—of this there is no doubt.
This task cannot be accomplished even by a Buddha in seven days. || 47 ||
The meditative concentration called the Vajra-Samaya-Command Wheel.
One should visualize Vairocana, who resides in the center of the element of space, adorned with vajra-flames, and endowed with the excellence of all aspects. 48.
One should visualize the highly renowned Vajrasattvas, born from the samaya of the three times, holding in their hands a vajra dense with sparks. (49)

Having gathered together the beings arisen in the ten directions by means of the differentiation of the vajra-body, one should cause them to enter into one's own body through the application of light rays. (50)
The vibration of all vajras is the body [of reality] for those of supreme wisdom;
let all the Buddhas, whose nature is the yoga of body, speech, and mind, listen! 51.
I am the glorious Vajradhara; through the differentiation of the wheel of command, I emanate those born from the three bodies by means of the blazing vajra.
If one should transgress the pledge, it will undoubtedly fall apart. || 52 ||
The samādhi called the Vajra of the Command of the Unpleasant Time.
One should contemplate the Buddha-maṇḍala-wielder situated in the center of the space-vajra;
one should fashion Yamāntaka as the great wheel, known as the space-vajra.
And having caused the Buddhas born in the three times to enter the mandala of the three bodies, one should again emanate the Buddhas who resemble the form of Yamāntaka. (54)
And one should visualize all beings born in the three times who have been slain by enemies of evil intent; this is the Vajra Command Maṇḍala. 55.
This is the samādhi called Sarvasamayasambhavayamāntakasamayatrikāyajñānavajra.

–52– By means of the vajras of body, speech, and mind, or by the quality of the meaning of one’s own mantra; or else, during the *pauṣpa* [flower] initiation, the turning of the wheel of command (*ājñācakra*). 56.
For the protection of all mantras of those who possess the supreme vajra of gnosis, this is declared for the purpose of protecting the awakening of all Buddhas. (57)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Bodhicitta:
"Having meditated upon the Dharma situated in the center of the space-vajra, which arises from the supreme Vairocana, one should fashion the seat, the foremost of the vajras of the three bodies. (58)
One should visualize the entire realm of space as completely filled with all the Buddhas;
one should conceive the gnosis of the mantra-syllables and phrases as the very form of the mind. (59)
Furthermore, one should emanate the Buddhas produced from the mind-vajra;
having thus formed the mind-vajra, one should cause them to enter into the three bodies.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra-Samaya of Space.
The samādhi named "Illuminator of the Jewel of Vajra Mantras."
One should visualize Vajrasattva, endowed with the excellence of all aspects;
having established the Buddhas in succession, one may walk upon the water.
By means of the application of the water of the pledge, one should visualize the feet upon the head. || 61 ||
Thus spoke the Blessed One, who is pure by nature.
The samādhi named "Treading upon the Vajra-Ocean."
Having meditated upon the Maheśvara maṇḍala, one should place the family of wrathful deities in its center;
one should visualize him with his head trampled by the feet of Karmavajra.
And thus he said:
The samādhi called "the vajra that paralyzes all proponents of other sects. || 62 ||
Having visualized all [the deities] in a wrathful form, with tips of three vajras resembling yellow filaments, one should contemplate them as being like the king of mountains upon one's head.
Even an army of Buddhas dies upon the pillar; there is no doubt about this.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the source of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The samādhi called "Paralyzing All Armies."
At the time of terrifying one's enemies, one should perform this meditation;
if a Buddha were to transgress it, he would burst apart—of this there is no doubt.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Trivajrasamaya:
"Having meditated upon the *hūṃ*-syllable as a stake (*kīlaka*) with the dimensions of five spears, one has thereby fashioned the Vajra-stake; one should visualize that within the heart."
Even the army of the Buddhas, when enraged, will undoubtedly go to destruction. || 65 ||
The samādhi called "the great destroyer of enemies."
Whether in a city, or in a village, or in a district, one should employ this [rite] constantly;
by this, there shall be perpetual peace, free from all diseases.
One should visualize a five-pronged vajra situated in the intermediate space;
having meditated upon it as being like the conflagration at the end of an aeon, one should then direct the reabsorption.
Furthermore, one should perform a vibration with the radiance of jewels and wish-fulfilling gems;
one should indeed meditate on the Cloud of Dharma and bestow the consecration.
By this vajra of meditative concentration, even that which is difficult to fill becomes completely filled;
he shall become a glorious wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi), the accomplisher of the vajra of giving.
One should cause that to radiate forth with clouds of Buddhas, the great Dharmas, and Vajrasattvas. || 69 ||
The state that endures for three incalculable eons is empowered by all the Buddhas;
this is the stainless secret of the body of all the Buddhas. (70)
The samādhi called "the arising of the vajra that removes the diseases of all sentient beings."
Wherever one should practice the undertaking with the vajra of meditative concentration, by abiding in this yoga of meditation, one is empowered by the Buddhas. (71)
One should visualize the great king Dhvajāmṛta as a vajra-stake, resembling a mass of blazing sparks; one should drive it into the circle of the ten directions.
And thus he said: [54] —54— And so it was said.
This is the samādhi called Jagadvijayaśāntivajra (the Vajra of Peaceful Victory over the World).
One should contemplate the supreme peaceful maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having meditated upon the form of Vairocana, one should then place it within the heart.
One should visualize the element of space as completely filled with the foremost Locanās;
then, having withdrawn them into a mass of light rays, one should cast it down upon the object of the rite.
The practitioner should emit clouds of Buddhas from the openings at the tips of his pores;
then, indeed, those clouds of Buddhas bestow empowerment upon him.
By this, one becomes the glorious Vajrasamaya at that very moment. || 75 ||
The samādhi called the Array of Clouds of the Buddhas' Samaya.
One should contemplate the auspicious Mahendra-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having meditated upon the image as the supreme Dharma, one should then place it within the heart.
One should fill the delightful realm of the space-element with those known as Pāṇḍara;
one should withdraw [them] by means of a mass of rays, possessing the luster of a precious wish-fulfilling gem.
The practitioner should present that to the seeker residing in the abode of body, speech, and mind;
then, from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin, he should radiate clouds of jewels.
One should indeed meditate upon the Cloud of Dharma and bestow the consecration.
By means of this vajra of meditation, even that which is difficult to fill becomes completely filled;
it becomes the glorious wish-fulfilling gem, the accomplisher of the vajra of giving. || 79 ||
The samādhi called the Array of Clouds of the Dharma-Samaya.
One should visualize the mandalas of the vajra, moon, and sun situated in the center of the space-element;
one who desires [attainment] should place the supreme image of the Vajradharma at the heart. 80.
The circle of space is completely filled with Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
by means of the application of five rays of light, one should cause splendor to descend upon that [place]. (81)
At that very moment, he would become pleasing to all the Buddhas;
resembling Mañjuśrī himself, he would become a performer of the deeds of others.
With a joyful heart and great eagerness, he bestows consecration;
he brings all people under his control merely by being seen, as they are impelled [by his power]. (83)
The samādhi called the Array of Clouds of Jewel Samayas.
One should visualize the space-vajra as filled with cruel and fierce rākṣasas, extremely terrible in their wrath, along with various jackals, crows, vultures, and dogs. (84)
One should always visualize the enemies as situated within a fire mandala; having meditated thus upon the wrongdoer of all Buddhas, one should apply the yoga. (85)
One should visualize the enemy as being completely drawn out, consisting of entrails, marrow, blood, and so forth;
then, attacked by those bearing various weapons, the enemy dies. (86)
Whether it be a Buddha or even a Vajradhara who is manifested by this [practice], he will die within the completion of half a month; of this there is no doubt. || 87 ||
The samādhi named the Array of the Vajra Cloud Samaya.
One should visualize Vairocana with three faces, possessing a radiance like the stalk of an autumn lotus,
white, black, and deep red, adorned with a crown of matted hair.
One should visualize the three-faced Vajrin, whose faces are black, red, and white; he wears a crown of matted locks, is blazing, and pervades the entire world-system. (89)
One should contemplate the three-faced one who is impassioned, with faces red, black, and white;
by meditating upon him as adorned with a crown of matted hair, one certainly attains success.
One should visualize a wheel, a vajra, and a great lotus in the right hands;
one should visualize six auspicious vajra-arms bearing various weapons. (91)
One should contemplate Locanā, who desires the welfare of all sentient beings; one should visualize her as having three faces—white, black, and deep red—and possessing a beautiful form. (92)
One should always meditate upon the Great Queen Khavajranetrī, who has three faces;
one should visualize her as having black, red, and white forms, and possessing a beautiful appearance. (93)
One should always meditate upon Vāgvajrī, the Great Queen, who has three faces;
one should visualize her as having a beautiful complexion, appearing red, white, and black. (94)
Meditating upon the Vidyā who holds a vajra and an utpala, who has three faces and is endowed with beautiful radiance, appearing yellow, black, and white, one shall attain primordial wisdom. 95.
One should visualize Yamāntaka, the great wrathful deity, with three faces, intensely radiant and fierce, the terror even of fear itself, sharp and black in color. (96)
One should contemplate Aparājita, the great wrathful deity, who utters a loud, mocking laugh; he has three faces, is dense with sparks, and is radiantly blazing. (97)
One should always meditate through yoga upon Hayagrīva, the great wrathful one, who arises like the conflagration at the end of an eon, possessing three faces and treading upon the wicked. (98)
Vajrāmṛta, the great wrathful one, whose mind is filled with sparks, resembling a blazing vajra, cruel, and the instiller of fear even in fear itself. || 99 ||
One should visualize the great wrathful deity Ṭakkirāja, who has three faces that bestow the three fears, four arms, and is the foremost among those who inspire terror. 100.

One should always meditate upon the three-faced one, who possesses great strength and the great vajra, who upholds the welfare and purpose of the three worlds, and who is the destroyer of all malevolent beings. (101)
One should visualize the Great Wrathful One Nīladaṇḍa, who instills fear in the three worlds, possessing three faces, arisen from the three vajras, and emitting sharp flames. 102.
The practitioner should meditate upon the great wrathful Vajrācala, squinting, born of the vajra, holding a sword and a noose, gentle, and three-faced. (103)
One should meditate upon the Vajrin, who is the single-syllable Mahoṣṇīṣa, blazing forth in all directions, with three faces, within the maṇḍala of meditation. 104.

One should meditate upon Sumbha, the bearer of the supreme gnosis, who is fierce and possesses a radiance like a sea of fear; he has three faces, his body is ablaze with flames, and he shines with the splendor of meditative concentration. 105.
The Tejorāśi-jayoṣṇīṣa and those others who are the Vajra-holders of Mantra—these should each be meditated upon through these enjoyments of the samaya. 106.
Innumerable samādhis have been proclaimed for the mantras; however, they are distinguished by the multiplicity of each individual wrathful deity. 107.
One should contemplate the supreme, translucent maṇḍala situated in the center of the element of space;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should manifest Vairocana. 108.
Transparent, resembling the moon, peaceful, and possessing a radiance equal to various rays of light, it has arisen like a mirror, [reflecting] the mandala of the triple world. 109.
Having visualized [the deity] adorned with all ornaments, he beholds awakening; by this, the majesty of the Buddha brings all sentient beings under his control. 110.
It is attained in this very life through the cultivation of the vajra of meditative concentration.
The samādhi named "The Beautiful Vajra Arising from the Samaya of Vairocana. || 111 ||
One should contemplate the supreme vajra-maṇḍala situated in the center of the sphere of space;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should visualize Vajrasattva. (112)
Resembling a pure body, wrathful, with a radiance equal to various flames, endowed with the excellence of all forms, and adorned with every ornament. (113)
Having meditated upon the peaceful state of gnosis, one shall attain the state of the swift Vajra;
by this, the majesty of the Vajra brings all sentient beings under control. 114.
This is attained in this very life through the application of the vajra of meditative concentration.
This is the samādhi called "The Beautiful Vajra Arising from the Samaya of All Vajras. || 115 ||
One should contemplate the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala situated within the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should contemplate the Dharma-sattva. || 116 ||
One should visualize [himself] as the Great Vajra of Cloud-like Radiance, possessing a pure body, gentle, adorned with all ornaments, and emitting shimmering rays of light. 117.
—58— By this, one attains in this very life the majesty of the Dharma, which arises from the indivisibility of the three bodies, and is adorned by the ocean of primordial wisdom. 118.
The samādhi called "the beautiful vajra arising from the commitment of the Dharma-sattva."
One should contemplate the supreme mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra; having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should visualize Locanā, the foremost of goddesses. 119.
She has a beautiful face and large eyes, is adorned with various ornaments,
is endowed with all auspicious marks, and bears the foremost of the three bodies.
One should manifest the wheel in the hand, which brings the three realms under control;
it is the knowledge that accomplishes all siddhis and bestows the wish-fulfilling jewel.
This is the samādhi called Locanāsamayājñānahastāgravatī (Possessing the Foremost Hand of the Wisdom of Locanā’s Samaya).
One should contemplate the supreme moon mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest the Space-Vajra Lady. 122.

One should meditate upon her who has a beautiful face, large eyes, and a luster like that of a blue lotus; she is endowed with all auspicious marks and possesses a neck as slender as the waist of an elephant. 123.
In his hand [he holds] a blue lotus and a wheel, honored by the three realms;
it is divine, the secret that brings about the awakening of a Buddha for the Vajra-holders of accomplishment. 124.
There is a samādhi called "Delighting with the Thunderbolt Clouds of the Rays of the Sun.
One should contemplate the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-thunderbolt;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest the Dharmavajrī. 125.
She has a beautiful face and wide eyes, resembling the finest ruby;
she is born from the tip of the net of illusion and is most dear to him who is colored by passion.
She is complete with all the primary marks and adorned with every ornament;
in her hand she holds a divine red lotus, empowered by all the Buddhas.
The divine source of the knowledge of phenomena, the secret of those who hold the vajra of the samaya. -59-
The samādhi called "the vajra that perceives the complete awakening to the reality of the dharma-samaya."
One should contemplate the supreme maṇḍala of accomplishment situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should then manifest Tārā as the foremost. 128.
Having meditated upon her who has a beautiful face and large eyes, adorned with various ornaments, resembling the color of gold, and eager with feminine guile and passion; 129.
One should clearly manifest in the hand a blue lotus resembling the color of gold, born from the vajra-samādhi and honored by all sentient beings. 130.
The samādhi called Samayatārāgravatī.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should visualize the foremost Yamāntaka. 131.
The circle of existence (bhava-maṇḍala) is blazing, dense with sparks, and full of wrath.
One should visualize him with red eyes, formidable with fangs, and holding a sword in his hand. || 132 ||
Having meditated upon the station of Vairocana in the crown, the Vajra-holders are satisfied;
for this is the commitment (samaya) of all the Wrathful Ones who possess the Vajra of Gnosis. 133.
This is the samādhi called the Array of the Radiant Manifestation of Yamāntaka.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest the one known as Aparājita.
One should visualize [the deity] as white in color, blazing with a dense mass of sparks, girdled by serpents, and possessing a terrifying, hideous face. 135.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, the Vajrins are pleased;
for this is the samaya of all the wrathful ones who possess the Vajra of Gnosis. 136.
The samādhi called the Invincible Vajra Array.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should manifest Hayagrīva. || 137 ||
One should visualize [him] as red in color, filled with sparks, wrathful, and flashing forth in all directions, treading upon all wicked beings. (138)
Having meditated upon the Buddha Amitābha upon the crown, the Vajra-holders are satisfied;
for this is the pledge (*samaya*) of all the Wrathful Ones who possess the Vajra of Gnosis. 139.
The samādhi named "The Array of the Arising and Manifestation of Aśvaghoṣa."
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest Vajrāmṛta.
One should visualize [him] as dense with sparks, blazing, filled with clouds of vajras, wrathful, full of rage, black, and possessing sharp fangs. 141.
Having visualized Akṣobhya’s pledge [deity] upon the crown, the wrathful one is pleased;
for this is the pledge of all wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. || 142 ||
The samādhi named Amṛtasamayasambhavavajra.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having visualized the form of a Buddha, one should manifest the being Ṭakkirāja.
One should visualize [the deity] as fierce, with disheveled hair-tips, terrifying even to fear itself,
adorned with all ornaments, and possessing the brilliant luster of a vajra.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction, this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. || 145 ||
The samādhi called "Delight in the Perfect Awakening of the Vajra of Dhyāna."
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the mouth;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest the One of Great Power. 146.
One should meditate upon the powerful Vajrin as fierce, wrathful, and holding a noose, within the blazing maṇḍala that is the abode of the three vajras and dense with sparks. 147.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction, this is indeed the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. (148) -61-
The samādhi named *Tribalavajra*.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest the blue vajra. 149.
One should meditate upon the wielder of the staff and the vajra as having a fierce black form, increasing the black ocean, blazing with a dense mass of sparks, and radiant.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction, this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. (151)
The samādhi called Vajradaṇḍasamayāgravatī.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra; having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should visualize the foremost Acala. 152.
One should meditate upon the immovable Vajrin as squinting, deformed, and wrathful, brandishing a noose and a sword, dense with sparks, and blazing. 153.
Having meditated on the Akṣobhya-samaya within the crown, which increases satisfaction, this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. (154)
The samādhi called "Treading upon the Foundation of the Vajra-Dhātu Pledge."
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should visualize the wheel of knowledge (vidyā-cakra). 155.
One should visualize the Uṣṇīṣacakrasamaya, complete with all the [major] marks, surrounded by a blazing wheel, and radiating light. 156.
Having visualized Akṣobhya’s pledge-form in the crown, which increases satisfaction, this is indeed the pledge of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. (157)
The samādhi called the Uṣṇīṣa-Vidyācala-Cakra.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having visualized the form of a Buddha, one should manifest Vajrasumbha. 158.

Meditating upon him whose body consists of sharp, blazing rays, who possesses a thunderbolt amidst the clouds, who holds a vajra in his hand, and who is of great radiance—one shall attain accomplishment. 159.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction, this is indeed the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress. (160)
The samādhi named Vajrasamayaśumbhavajra.
By means of the wheel of the cessation of anger, which serves the wheel of the Buddhas, the vajra-knowledges of meditative absorption are accomplished from the vajra-maṇḍala. 161.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Awakening through the Meditation on the Reality of the Array of Samayas," in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Chapter Fourteen: Then the Blessed One, Mahāvajradhara, the Lord of the Samayas of all Tathāgatas, entered the meditative absorption named "The Supreme Samaya of Peace" and emitted this Consort of all Tathāgatas from the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
Oṃ ru ru sphuru jvala tiṣṭha Siddhilocane, O you who accomplish all aims, svāhā!
Then, as soon as this song had been sung, all those wise ones who possess every perfection were satisfied and attained great joy, recollecting the Buddha-vajra.
She is the mother who generates peace for the Buddhas, the accomplisher of all activities,
the one proclaimed as the reviver of the dead, and the stimulator of the Vajra-samaya.
And so he said:

Then the Blessed One, the Wrathful Vajra of the Samaya of the Three Bodies, entered the meditative absorption named “The Vajra of the Samaya of Existence and Non-existence,” and from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, he brought forth this supreme queen of all Vajra-holders.
Oṃ! O Śaṅkarī, O Śāntikarī, Ghuṭṭa, Ghuṭṭanī! Strike, strike, Ghuṭṭanī! Svāhā!
Then, as soon as this song was sung, she whose eyes were beautifully blossoming, while recollecting the Vajra-Mind, [became one] with the indestructible vajra of the Three Vajras. (3)
In the applications of the protection-vajra, she is always the accomplisher of rites;
she is known as the constant bestower of strength to those afflicted by the fear of the great vajra.

Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption called "The Observation of the Great Passion Samaya" and emitted this supreme consort of the Dharma-body from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
Oṃ kaṭe vikaṭe kaṭaṅkaṭe karoṭavīrye svāhā!
Then, as soon as this song had been sung, the Holder of the Supreme Vajradharma,
being pleased, entered meditative absorption while recollecting Vajradharma.
—64— By the mere recitation [of this mantra], according to the word of Vāgvajra, it constantly brings about the nourishment of the Dharma and strength, and always possesses a great treasury. || 6 ||
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Samantasambhavavajra and emitted this supreme consort of the Samayasattva from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
Oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā.
Then, as soon as this had been sung, all the great-souled Buddhas were filled with joy and attained gnosis while recollecting the vajra-body.
The great army of the Buddha-vajra brings the entire realm of sentient beings under its power from all sides; it makes them all like servants, rendered motionless, in an instant. 8.

And so it is said: Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called the Vajra Array of Clouds of Stainless Rays and emitted from his own vajras of body, speech, and mind this great wrathful deity Vajrayamāntaka.

Homage to the Vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all! Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi! O subduer of all the wicked, you who hold a sword, a mace, an axe, and a noose in your hands; four-faced one, four-armed one, six-legged one, come, come! O destroyer of the life-force of all the wicked, great destroyer of obstacles, deformed-faced one, terrifier of all spirits, you who sound the loud, echoing laugh, you who are clothed in a tiger skin: perform, perform all rites! Cut, cut all mantras! Pierce, pierce the supreme mudrās! Draw them forth!

Draw forth all beings! Grind, grind all the wicked! Enter, enter into the center of the maṇḍala! O ender of the life of Vaivasvata, accomplish my task! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Do not delay, do not delay! Remember your pledge! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ! Shatter, shatter! O fulfiller of all hopes, destroy all enemies! Act, act! O Blessed One, why do you tarry? Accomplish, accomplish all my aims! SVĀHĀ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the Buddhas of great renown became afraid, their minds terrified, as they recollected the Vajra-mind.
Having obtained a skull that is free of cracks, beautiful in form, and possessed of wisdom, and having placed it so as to be stepped upon by his feet while recollecting this mantra: || 10 ||
By reciting Locanā and Māmakī, who belong to the great Vajra family,
two or three times, she is certainly drawn forth in an instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Bodhicittavajra.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocanavajra, entered the samādhi called Samayaraśmighanāgra and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this Amṛtasamayavajrakrodha: "Homage to the omnipresent vajras of body, speech, and mind!"

Homage to Vajrakrodha, the Great Fierce One with formidable fangs, who holds a sword, a mace, an axe, and a noose in his hands. Oṃ! Amṛtakuṇḍalin! Kha kha! Eat, eat! Stay, stay! Bind, bind! Slay, slay! Burn, burn! Roar, roar! Burst asunder, burst asunder! To the one who brings an end to the life of Mahāgaṇapati and all obstructors and Vināyakas, svāhā!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the Buddhas of great renown fell into a swoon and were seized by fear, recollecting their vajra-bodies.
In all applications of mantras, and in the rite of vajra-expulsion,
one personally expels even the army of the Buddhas by means of the prescribed ritual.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, entered the meditative absorption called *Buddharaśmivajra* and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this great wrathful deity Vajrāparājita:
*Namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇām | oṃ hūṃ jina-ṛti he hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā ||*
Then, as soon as this was sung, all the Buddhas of great renown became afraid, their minds trembling with terror, as they recollected the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).

In places filled with fierce *rākṣasas*, beasts of prey, and cruel beings, and crowded with great terrors, one performs the ritual action according to the rules while recollecting the Vajra-mind. (15)
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, entered the samādhi called *Amitasambhavavajra* and emitted this Lotus-Born Vajra-Wrathful Deity from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind:
*Namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇām | Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ tarula virula sarvaviṣaghātaka jvalitavisphuliṅgāṭṭāṭṭahāsa kesarisaṭāṭopaṭaṅkāravajrakhuranirghātanacalitavasudhātala niśvāsamāruto...*

O you who shake the earth, O terrifying one with loud, boisterous laughter, O you of immeasurable strength and prowess, O you inhabited by the hosts of the Noble Ones and terrified throngs of spirits! Buddha! Buddha! Hayagrīva! Devour, devour the mantras of others! Cut them asunder, cut them asunder! Grant me success! Cause [the mantra] to descend! Be unimpeded against all fevers, thirst, and the like, and against all seizing spirits! O Vajradaṃṣṭra, why do you delay? [Devour] this entire host of wicked seizing spirits and wicked assemblies!

Or: *dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna matha matha maṭa maṭa ghātaya ghātaya bandha bandha! Perform the action authorized by the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha quickly! To Hayagrīva, phaṭ! To Vajragātra, phaṭ! To Vajranetra, phaṭ! To Vajradaṃṣṭra, phaṭ! To Vajrakhura, phaṭ! To Vajrakhuranirghātana, phaṭ! To the destroyer of supreme mantras, phaṭ! To the one who causes terror in the three worlds, phaṭ! To the one unimpeded in all actions, phaṭ! To the terrifier of the Vajra family, phaṭ! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
Then, as soon as he had emerged, the great elder sisters, Dharmavajrā and the others,
became terrified and fell into a swoon, recollecting the King of Gnosis.
By the impelling of the King of Wrath, he makes the entire realm of space— which is filled with poison and has the luster of the vajra-hālāhala— completely free of poison.

And so it is said: Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, having entered the samādhi called Amoghasamayasambhavaketuvajra, emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this King of Wrathful Deities, Nīlavajradaṇḍa.
Homage to the Vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all!

Oṃ, come, come, Blessed One, Blue Vajra-staff! Turu turu, hulu hulu, hā hā, gulu gulu! Subdue, subdue! Tread upon, tread upon, Blessed One, with the speed of the wind! Quickly burn, burn the spirits! Rend, rend! Carry away, carry away! Cook, cook! Churn, churn! Cast down, cast down! Maṭṭa maṭṭa, subdue, subdue! Perform the subduing of all activities! Cut, cut! Devour, devour! You who delight in fat, flesh, blood, marrow, and grease!
Come, come, O Blessed One! Destroy, destroy all obstacles, all mantras, all root-rites, and all root-grahas! Shatter, shatter! Crush, crush! Accomplish this task for me! HŪṂ!

To the Blue One, to the one with the blue vajra-staff! Turu turu, to the destroyer of obstacles and Vināyakas! Huru huru, to the blazing and fierce one! Torment the hearts of all enemies! Cut, cut! You who sever all spells!

HŪṂ! Remember, remember the remaining sciences and the pledge; by the word of Vajradhara, cut through all karmas! HŪṂ HŪṂ! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Act, act! Turu turu! Huru huru! PHAṬ PHAṬ! HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ! Cause to be devoured by Kṛtānta, the one who terrifies gods and ṛṣis! Strike, strike! To Vajradaṇḍa, SVĀHĀ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all those born from the foremost of the wicked,
terrified and with agitated minds, called to mind Vajrasattva.
By reciting this King of Wrath of great renown one hundred and eight times, he becomes the slayer of all evil beings through the application of ritual methods and the wheel [of power]. (19)
And so it is said:
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhyavajra, having entered the meditative absorption named Samantameghaśrī, emitted this Mahābalavajra from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind:
*Namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇām*.

Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ ūgraśūlapāṇi hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ jyotirnirṇāda hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ oṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ | Oṃ mahābalāya svāhā. Immediately upon these words being spoken, all the nāgas of great power became terrified and agitated in mind, recollecting the vajra of the three bodies.
By the mere application of recitation, one shall accomplish all rites;
and during a time of drought, one shall cause a circle of water to fall.
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Samantanirghātavajra and emitted this Great Wrathful King Ṭakkirāja of all the Tathāgatas from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind:
*Namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇām | oṃ ṭakki hūṃ jaḥ*.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the great-souled Buddhas became afraid and entered into the pledge (samaya), recollecting the body of the three vajras.
By means of the right foot, through the application of Vajrasattva, and by the wheel of the three vajra-mantras, there shall be the summoning of all sentient beings. (23)
Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption named Jñānamālāmbuvajra, emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this Acalavajracaṇḍasamaya.
Homage to the Vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all!

Oṃ acalakāraṇa hūṃ hūṃ moṭṭa moṭṭa saṭṭa saṭṭa ha ha moha moha saha saha hana hana daha daha taṭṭa taṭṭa tiṣṭha tiṣṭha āviśa āviśa mahāmattapālaka dhuna dhuna tiṇi tiṇi kiṇi kiṇi khāda khāda vighnān māraya māraya duṣṭān bhakṣa bhakṣa sarvān kuru kuru kiri kiri mahāviṣamavajra sphoṭaya sphoṭaya!

HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ! O dancer who performs with human strength! ĀṂ ĀṂ HĀṂ HĀṂ! O you of immovable mind, burst asunder, burst asunder! OṂ ASAMANTIKA TRĀṬ! O you of great power, satisfy the pledge! MAṂ TRĀṂ HĀṂ MĀṂ! May it be purified! May the Vajra-holder be pleased; homage be to those of irresistible power! JVĀLAYA TRĀṬ! O Unbearable One, homage! SVĀHĀ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the gods together with their attendants fainted, their minds filled with terror, as they recollected the mantra-body.
By means of this wrathful mantra, even Mahādeva and other gods, though possessed of great supernatural powers, are drawn forth in terror with their bodies folded in submission. (25)
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Samayavijṛmbhitavajra and, from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, emitted this Sumbha Mahākrodha, the pledge of all Vajradharas:
Oṃ namaḥ samantakāyavākcittavajrāṇām | Oṃ sumbha nisumbha hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya ho bhagavan vidyārāja hūṃ phaṭ ||
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the maidens, possessing great supernatural powers, had their hair disheveled and their bodies naked as they recollected Vajrasattva. (26)
Trampling upon the feet of Vajrasattva, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, he performs the supreme summoning of the Vajra-maidens with the vajra-hook and noose. (27)

Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption called “The Vajra Arising from the Reality of the Great Samaya” and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this word of reality concerning the secret speech-samaya of the great samaya-vajra: “The visualization of Vajrasattva within the three bodies of the Buddha-vajra is the supreme method for summoning the Buddhas by means of those who hold the noose, the vajra, and the hook. (28)
Through the union of the Buddha’s speech and body, and by means of the practice of the great wheel, Vajrasattva, the Great King, is always and certainly drawn forth. (29)
Through the great wheels, lotuses, and vajras, by means of the meditations on the indivisibility of the three vajras,
and through the various applications of the vajra-hook, the summoning of all mantras is certain.
Having meditated upon one's own mantra-person as auspicious and consisting entirely of vajra, [one should draw] an excellent human maiden by means of the yoga of the heart-vajra-hook. (31)
When joined with the whirlwind, one is always surely drawn [upward];
one should meditate on the great image of Vairocana as a moon mandala. (32)
One should contemplate Śacī stationed there through the application of the Vajrāmṛta mantra;
by reciting it fifty times, she is certainly and always drawn forth.
Having meditated upon the great image of the Vajrāṅkuśa, possessing a radiance equal to sharp flames, and the vajra-maṇḍala, one performs the supreme summoning of the celestial maidens. 34.
One's own Krodhavajra-samaya, who dwells in the Vajra-pātāla, performs the supreme summoning of the daughters of the Daityas with his trident, vajra, hook, and noose. (35)
Alternatively, by means of the application of the vajra-hook, one should place either red chalk or white chalk in the mouth at the time of a lunar eclipse and perform the practice.
If one should write down the name of him who [is the master] of Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, and the gods,
they will come forth terrified by fear, as if by a word that is a thunderbolt.
One should visualize Mañjuvajra, endowed with the excellence of all aspects; one should contemplate the great wrathful Yamāntaka as the vajra-hook.
"Having meditated upon the great wheel of the conflagration at the end of an eon, one should accomplish the yakṣīs.
Thus he said.
Through the differentiation of mudrās and in every way through the differentiation of mantras, the stage of summoning is proclaimed; otherwise, one would meet with destruction. (39)
Vajrasattva, the great king, is to be exhorted again and again;
he alone is the king of all mantras, the supreme and eternal one. (40)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption named Samantavijṛmbhatajñānavajra, emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this supreme Vajra of Speech, the Great Serpent Aparājita, named Vajraikajaṭā: Oṃ śūlini svāhā!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, the naga maidens of great supernatural power,
their naked bodies burning, recollected the awakening of the Buddha.
By means of this mantra-vidyā, all serpents are summoned;
one may summon and enjoy the company of a large-eyed Naga maiden. 42.
Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named Gaganasamayasambhavavajra and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this Great Dharma-Samaya-Vajra-Bhrkuti:
OM BHAYANĀŚĀNI TRĀSANI TRĀSAYA BHRKUTĪ TAṬI VETAṬI VAIRAṬI VAIRAṬI ŚVETE SVETAJAṬINI SVĀHĀ.
Then, as soon as this was sung, all the daughters of the Vidyādharas trembled and were seized with fear, recollecting the King of Knowledge.
Having drawn forth the great maiden of the Vidyādharas, who wears swaying golden earrings, by means of this mantra-vidyā and the pledge (samaya),
through the perfected and most beautiful King of Obstructing Vajras; 44.
Born from the three vajra-gnoses, they are drawn forth from all directions in an instant. || 45 ||
Alternatively, for all wrathful deities, it is taught that by reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times,
the practitioner’s [mantras] become performers of all rites in great, secluded places.
Those intent on reviling their preceptor and those who revile the supreme Mahāyāna should be diligently executed by death, or else they should be expelled from their station. (47)
By this, one shall attain supreme enlightenment and the accomplishment of mantra; thus he said.
It is the destruction of the body, speech, and mind of all the Buddhas of the ten directions. || 48 ||
One should perform the meditation according to the prescribed rite upon enemies of evil intent;
one should cause [the image] to be made wet with blood, wet with water, or even wet with feces and urine. (49)
Having donned the insignia and having invoked the King of Wrath, one should employ it;
when the hundred and eight [recitations] are complete, even a Buddha will certainly be destroyed.
And so it is said:
"Having soaked a cloth in water and tied it with the foremost bond of wrath, and having stepped upon the *liṅga* with one's foot, even a Buddha will certainly perish. (51)
Having wrapped oneself in a cloth soaked with feces and urine, which is foul-smelling and loathsome, one should repeat the mantra; [the enemy] dries up and dies in an instant.
Having put on a garment soaked with ashes and water, and being filled with wrath, even Vajrasattva himself would be shattered by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times. 53.
And so it is said: "Having wrapped himself in a garment moistened with water, with a mind full of rage, naked and with hair disheveled, he becomes one of hideous and fierce agitation. (54)
"Having stepped upon the *liṅga* with one's foot, one may even destroy the *khadhātu*. Thus he said:
"In the mother’s house, in a cremation ground, in an empty dwelling, or at a crossroads... (55)
Or, at a solitary linga or a single tree, one should commence the rite of malevolent magic (*abhicāra*).
A stake made of human bone, measuring eight finger-breadths in length, [should be used]. (56)
Having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one should conceal it at the gates of the enemies.
The Buddha, the bestower of the three bodies, is devoid of both knowledge and ignorance. || 57 ||
Within half a fortnight, one who has reached a fully formed *kapāla*—especially if he is wise—either falls away [from his state] or even dies. (58)

One should write the mantra-syllables there and cause them to be recited with the Vajra-speech; whether at the gate of an enemy or in a village, [the enemy] is certainly driven away by means of concealment.
One should inscribe the Krodha-mantra on a palm leaf or elsewhere;
whether at the enemy's house or at the door, [the enemy] perishes or withers when it is kept hidden.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāsamayaketuvajra. Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named the Vajra of Binding the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas, and from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, he brought forth this Vajra Stake of the Body, Speech, and Mind of the Entire Triple World.

Oṃ gha gha, slay, slay all the wicked ones, phaṭ! Stake, stake all the sinful ones, phaṭ! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! O Vajra, stake [them]! Vajradhara commands the vajra of body, speech, and mind: stake [them]! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the Vajras of great supernatural power fainted and were overcome with fear, recollecting the Mind of the Space-Vajra.
A kila made of human bone, or produced from the tip of khadira wood, or a kila fashioned from iron, destroys the body of the three vajras. (62)
Having concentrated upon Vajrasattva, who is brilliantly radiant and filled with sparks,
one should meditate on the image extending to the three vajra-bodies and then apply it.
Having meditated upon the great mudrā of Vairocana, or that of Rāgavajrin,
or the great mudrā of Yamāntaka, one performs the triple vajra-stake.
By means of the *vajra* of the *kuṇḍala-mṛta*, the severing of the wicked and cruel must be performed through the *vajra-yoga*, even in the case of a great-souled Buddha.
From the heart down to the ends of the feet, one should visualize the vajra-stake; this manifestation of the stake is the samaya of the deity above. (66)
By means of the application of the meditation-vajra, even a Buddha is certainly pinned down;
the great king Vajrasattva, being pinned down, dies quickly.

Then the Blessed One Mahāvairocana entered the samādhi called "Vajra of the Physical Manifestation" and, from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, uttered this mantra for the vajra-stake that summons the commitment of his own body:
*Oṃ chinda chinda bhinda bhinda hana hana daha daha dīptavajracakra kṣūṃ phaṭ*.
The form of mutual entwining, with the joining of the thumbs and feet, is the treading upon the foot of Vairocana and the striking down of the vajra-stake. || 68 ||
As soon as the Mahāsattva has been struck, he shall arise by means of the foremost commitment (*samaya*); otherwise, he will incur the state of destruction. (69)

Then the Blessed One, the Lord of the World, having entered the samādhi called "The Manifestation of Speech," emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this mantra for the impaling stake that brings about the commitment of speech: OṂ VĀK-SAMAYA-ĀKṢEPAKĪLANA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Oṃ hnīḥ bhūr bhuvaḥ.
Placing the vajra-finger upon the lotus of blossoming gnosis, one treads upon the words of the Vajra-speech and strikes down the vajra-stake. || 70 ||
As soon as the Great Vajra is struck, he who has arisen from the abode of the three bodies shall rise up by that very act of being struck; otherwise, he would meet with destruction. (71)

Then the Blessed One, Mahāvajradhara, entered the samādhi called “The Vajra of the Mind’s Expansion” and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this mantra for the impelling stake of the mind-commitment:
Oṃ vajrarāja hūṃ.
By means of the placement of the five-pronged [vajra], the ritual procedure is filled with sparks;
it consists of treading upon the state of the Mind-Vajra and the striking down of the Vajra-stake. 72.
As soon as the Great Vajra is struck, he who is born from the abode of the three vajras shall rise up by that very striking; otherwise, he would meet with destruction. (73)

By means of the path of correct ritual application through the yoga of body, speech, and mind, one shall nail down [the obstructors] as far as the vajra of the space-element; of this there is no doubt. (74)

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahākīlavajra. Then the Buddhas, the foremost of the three bodies, who desire the welfare of the realm of sentient beings, being satisfied and having attained great joy, uttered this proclamation: || 75 ||
Oh, the supreme secret state! Oh, the collection of the essential core!
Oh, the peaceful state of Dharma! Oh, the shatterer of the vajra! 76.
The nailing down of all Buddhas is the nailing down of the Bodhisattvas of great renown;
it is proclaimed as the nailing down of the Vajras of body, speech, and mind. (77)
This is that nailing of all mantras, arising from reality;
it is the bestower of boons upon body, speech, and mind, the compendium of the reality of mantra.
Thus [ends the verse]. || 78 ||

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled “The King of the Manifestation of the Miraculous Mantras of Body, Speech, and Mind,” in the *Śrī Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the Ultimate Secret of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
Chapter Fifteen: Then Vajradhara, the King, the Great Immutable One of all space, the Omniscient One who bestows all empowerments, uttered the Vajra of Speech: 1.
Then Vajradhara, the King, the Great Immutable One of all space, the Omniscient One who bestows all empowerments, uttered the Vajra of Speech.
The practitioner should constantly cultivate that twelve-year-old daughter of the high-souled Caṇḍāla, especially in solitary places.
One should construct a square mandala there according to the rules, using feces, urine, and other substances, by means of the practices of the Vajramandala.
Having placed upon his lap one who is perfectly pure in all marks, with a beautiful face, most radiant,
and complete with all ornaments, he should meditate upon her.
Through the wheel of the five maṇḍalas, one should meditate on the visualization of the Buddha’s form; this is the delightful locus of worship, the secret of the mantra-vajra holders. (5)
By means of the application of meditation and mantra, one becomes equal in radiance to the Buddha, possessing the great image of Vairocana and the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
One should constantly practice with the daughter of the noble-minded washerman, who has the appearance of a blue lotus petal, through the application of Vajrasattva. (7)
Having performed that very conjunction with the ritual procedure, one should commence the rite;
for this is the commitment (samaya) of all mantras, which is difficult to transgress. (8)
At that very moment, he becomes equal in radiance to Vajrasattva, the King who upholds all dharmas and accomplishes both desire and liberation. || 9 ||
The practitioner should constantly accomplish the practice of a beautiful-faced, large-eyed, and most splendid dancing girl through the meditations on Vajradharma. (10)
He becomes the very essence of Vajradharma, established upon the ten stages; he is the King who upholds the vow of speech, the foremost of all, the supreme lord. (11)
One whose nature is the Vajra-dharma should win over a maiden born of a Śūdra family from among those of the Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, or Vaiśya castes; this brings about the secret [attainment]. 12.
When the vajra-sun has set, one should begin the practice;
at the time of sunrise, it is accomplished by those with the most excellent meditative cultivation. 13.
Having meditated upon the supreme Vajrasattva, complete with all ornaments and adorned with perfumes and flowers, one shall attain swift accomplishment. || 14 ||
He shall become a bestower of the three bodies, marked by the characteristics of a Buddha;
he emits a radiance extending for a hundred yojanas.
One should undertake all yogas through the application of the two organs;
for this is the inviolable commitment (samaya) of all accomplishments. 16.
If one desires the siddhi of the Vajra-holder, one should consume the sacrament of feces and urine;
for this is the samaya of all siddhis, which is difficult to transgress. (17)
Through the application of the two organs by means of the samaya of feces, urine, and so forth, the unsurpassed reality—the auspicious state of the awakening of the Buddhas—is accomplished. (18)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Kāmamokṣasamayavajra.
Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named Mahāsamayavajrakrodha and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this Vajra-terrifying Wrath of all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ hnīḥ ṣṭrīḥ vikṛtānana! Destroy all enemies! Paralyze them! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
One who is enraged should offer into a fire of thorns salt mixed with poison and blood, as well as black mustard seeds, together with the words of the maiden's name.
At midday or at midnight, this should be recited in every way;
the wise man should offer oblations eight thousand times according to the rule within a triangular fire-pit.
This rite should be performed for three days for the sake of the fruit [attained] by virgins;
by that means, immobilization (stambhana) occurs eternally, even for an incalculable number of three kalpas.
Whether it be a Buddha, a holder of the Dharma, or even Vajrasattva himself—
if one who is deluded in nature should transgress [this command], that shall be the end of his life.
Likewise, on the fourteenth or the eighth day, having taken charcoal from a cremation ground and consecrated it according to the ritual procedure, he shall always become a servant.
Having meditated upon it, the knower of mantras who draws a line after fashioning an image of any enemy whatsoever dies; of this there is no doubt. (24)
By means of the yoga of meditation, one should cause the mallet to fall, and once it has certainly fallen, one should visualize the syllable HŪṂ, joined with flames, as a blazing vajra. || 25 ||
The family of Vajrapāṇi is known as the destroyer of all evil-doers.
One should draw a man or a woman using chalk, charcoal, or similar materials. (26)
Having visualized an axe in one's hand, one should visualize one's own neck severed;
[thus do] the Buddhas, the supreme jewels of the three vajras, who desire the welfare of all sentient beings. (27)
By this, one is either struck or killed; of this there is no doubt.
It is the great blazing Karma-vajra, agitated by a dense mass of sparks. (28)
Having visualized a vajra in the center, there is the supreme subduing of water;
however, if wind and other disturbances should arise while the mandala is being drawn, [the following should be done]. (29)
Then, having formed the fang-mudrā, one should bring to mind a malevolent being, or whatever may have been emanated by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. (30)

If it does not perish upon merely being seen, yet should meet its destruction, then the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, and whatever other malevolent beings there may be, will be terrified by that mantra and die; of this there is no doubt. (31)
In this regard, here is the heart-essence of the secret mantra of all Tathāgatas:
By means of the application of the Gnosis-being, one should manifest the image in the center;
the knower of mantras should always place the woman in the four locations. (32)
Complete with all ornaments and endowed with all the [major] marks,
having extended the lotus, one should contemplate this mantra:
one should visualize the Yogavajrin as blazing with the radiance of five-colored rays.
By causing [the seed-syllable] to descend into the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one shall attain awakening. || 34 ||
At that very moment, he becomes equal in radiance to Vairocana;
he is the Great King Vajrasattva, the bearer of the vajra of the body of the Perfect Buddha.

There is a samādhi called "The Producer of All Beings. Having obtained a woman of beautiful countenance who is well-disposed toward one's welfare, one should begin the worship in a secluded place; one should consume the secret-of-secrets. (36)
At that very moment, he would become equal in splendor to Mañjuśrī, a glorious lord of invisibility, with a radiance like that of Jāmbūnada gold. (37)
One may cause food, or excrement, or even meat to enter [the mouth];
by consecrating it according to the ritual procedure, that food is no longer perceived by the Buddhas. (38)
And so it is said:
"Having taken the excrement according to the ritual procedure, one should place it within a hollowed vessel made of two earthenware bowls;
having empowered it one hundred and eight times with the Buddhas as suns, it becomes invisible. (39)
Having taken dog meat, horse meat, or "great meat" (human flesh) according to the prescribed rite,
and consuming them by means of the *sampuṭa* yoga, one is not seen by them.
A pill joined with feces and encased in the three metals, when applied by means of the two organs, cannot be seen even by all the Buddhas.
A pill joined with *mahāmāṃsa* (human flesh) and encased in the three metals... [41]
Through the application of the two organs, one is not seen by any of the Buddhas. || 42 ||
A pill prepared with one's own flesh and encased in the three metals, by the application of the two organs, cannot be seen even by all the Buddhas. (43)
A pill prepared with beef and encased in the three metals, through the application of the two organs, cannot be seen even by all the Buddhas. (44)
The practitioner should have pills made from insects born of excrement;
by the application of the two organs, he is not seen by any of the Buddhas. (45)
A pill prepared with camphor and sandalwood, encased in the three metals, is not seen by any of the Buddhas when employed through the union of the two organs. (46)
A pill composed of *rocanā* and *aguru*, encased in the three metals, when employed through the application of the two organs, makes one possess the great power of a *vajra*. (47)
A pill prepared with camphor and saffron, encased in the three metals, is not seen by any of the Buddhas when applied through the union of the two organs. (48)
And so it is said:
"By taking recourse to Mahāmudrā, whoever that Vajradhara may be, he shall become such a glorious one, possessing great strength and prowess. (49)
One whose movement is like a vajra shall traverse ten million yojanas above;
the glorious one shall possess the gait of the triple-thousandfold world system and a radiance equal to a Buddha. || 50 ||
The one of great power may desire a maiden dwelling in the realm of desire, enjoying celestial pleasures and observing the vows of her family, as well as one dwelling in the realm of form.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Vajra of the Vanishing of the Samaya.
Then the Buddhas, their souls delighted, their minds undeluded, and wise, with eyes wide open in wonder, uttered this proclamation: (52)
Oh, how truly wonderful is this! Oh, what a secret, the great syllable!
Oh, how pure by nature it is! Oh, how stainless is the Dharma!
Thus [ends the verse]. 53.
Then the Teacher Vajradhara— the creator, the maker, the great immutable one, the pure vajra, the great Dharma— produced the sound of the vajra.
Through the application of all vajras, there is the pleasing of the Buddhas who possess the vajra;
through the differentiation of the awakening of the Buddhas, there is the pleasing of those who practice with the vajra. || 55 ||

The propitiation of the Uṣṇīṣa is known to be accomplished through the forms of Vajralocanā and others; that cultivation of the Buddha-vajra is also the most excellent among the wrathful deities. (56)
The visualization of Ratnaketu among the supreme dharmas of the Vidyārājas;
the visualization of Amitāyus within the applications of the Vidyārājñīs. || 57 ||
The cultivation of unerring wisdom for all ritual mantras, and the visualization of Vajrasattva for all mantras whatsoever. (58)
And so it is said:
"The ritual manual of Yamāntaka for the mantras and tantras of the yakṣiṇīs, which effects the paralyzing and the fierce incitement of all yoga-mantras. (59)
And thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāsamayavajra:
"By means of this meditation-vajra, the mandala for the propitiation of mantras—the great samaya-sādhana—has been declared for the benefit of practitioners. (60)
Then the Teacher Vajradhara, the Lord and Master of all phenomena, purified in body, speech, and mind, uttered the Wisdom-Vajra: || 61 ||
On the delightful peaks of mountains and in solitary forests,
one should practice the vajra of meditation through the application of mantra recitation.
All [beings], such as Vajrasattva and the others, impelled by mantra and meditative concentration,
perform diverse activities just as spoken by the words of Vākyavajra.
The great image of Vajradharma has a radiance equal to a ruby;
it is the great vajra of body, speech, and mind, and therein one should conceive of the family.
By performing the entire ritual of possession, one certainly attains accomplishment.
Stobha-stambha, Mahābimba, Āryabhauma, and the fourth.
This must be performed by the Siddhivajra; thus, it is eternally accomplished.
[One should take] a twelve-year-old girl or a twelve-year-old man. (66)
One should perform the ritual of possession by grasping [the deity] who is complete with all the auspicious marks.
Having performed all the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the rite, otherwise one incurs ridicule among the beings within the three realms. 67.

In this regard, these are the syllables and words of the heart-mantra: HŪṂ HAḤ ĀḤ AIḤ. Even the element of space (khadhātu), which is motionless and devoid of all conceptual constructions, Vajrasattva himself causes to enter [into a state of possession] by means of the ritual procedure. (68)
In the syllable HŪṂ is the essence of Vajrasattva; in the syllable HAḤ is the Body-Vajra;
in the syllable ĀḤ is the King who holds the Dharma—this is the firm secret word. (69)
The utterance of the syllable "aiḥ" is declared to be a *stobha*; it is remembered as causing whirling and trembling.
Indeed, this is proclaimed as the secret among all *stobhas*.
And so it is said:
"Impelled by the King of Vajras, they arise— terrified with fear— measuring one cubit, two cubits, or up to five or eight cubits."
In that very same way, everything here which brings about the secret [state] is just as before.
Thus [ends the verse]. 71.
Then King Vajradhara, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, uttered this sound, which is the resonance of the state of the three bodies: || 72 ||
Even by those whose minds are not one-pointed, this task—the rending of all evil ones—must be performed with firm vows or through another yoga. (73)
Having fashioned an image of the enemy out of charcoal, chaff, and other such materials,
one should, being naked and with hair disheveled, destroy even the three worlds.

Having fashioned an image of the enemy with the ashes from a funeral pyre in a cremation ground, [if one recites the mantra] one hundred and eight times a thousand times, he dies; of this there is no doubt. (75)
By means of beef, horse meat, and variegated dog meat, one should perform [the rite] within a triangular mandala; even Vajra himself will certainly perish.
The destruction of all [obstacles] through human flesh is known as the Vajra-born;
for this is remembered as the terrible destroyer of all cruel beings. (77)

Having fashioned an image of the enemy using excrement and urine from one who has attained the highest stage (*agradharmin*), one should, filled with wrath, offer it into a fire of thorns; even a Buddha will certainly perish.
And so it is said:
"Having fashioned an image of the enemy, even at the flow of a river or a mountain stream,
one should pierce every limb, down to the size of a sesame seed, with thorns produced from poison."
If one fills [the verse] with injunctive words, even a Buddha will certainly perish.
And so it is said:
"Mustard seed, salt, oil, poison, and likewise thorn-apple—this is remembered as the most excellent means for the slaying of all Buddhas. (80)
Having wrapped oneself in a cloth soaked in glowing coals with a mind full of anger,
and having stepped upon the *liṅga* with one's foot, one will certainly be seized by the *rākṣasas*.
Having fashioned an effigy with powdered bone, poison, and blood,
even the formidable Vajrasattva is swiftly seized.
Combined with a *liṅga* and *rājika* salt, and filled even with feces and urine,
it is seized by Mahāmegha once it has been stepped upon with the foot.
And so it is said:
"In this regard, this is the heart-mantra of the Great Wrathful Samaya of the Vajra of All Tathāgatas."
Homage to the Vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all!

Oṃ hūlū hūlū! Stay, stay! Bind, bind! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Roar, roar! Burst asunder, burst asunder! To the one who brings an end to the life of Mahāgaṇapati and all obstructors and impediments: Hūṃ phaṭ!
Whether it be fire-offering or meditation that distinguishes body, speech, and mind, this supreme rite of slaying must be performed with no other state of mind. 84.
Having meditated upon Vajrasattva, who is exceedingly fierce, formidable, and terrifying, with an axe and a mallet in his hands, one should perform the visualization. (85) -83-
In this regard, here is the samaya of the Great Fierce Wrath.
One should visualize the realm of the dead completely filled with all the Buddhas;
having meditated that it has been destroyed by that evil one, [the victim] would die at that very moment. (86)
One should visualize it as being completely filled with Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
when struck by all the wicked ones, Vajradhara himself dies.
The practitioner of mantra should visualize before him an enemy who has harmed the Buddha;
he should imagine that [enemy] terrified and overwhelmed by fear, and he will die—of this there is no doubt. (88)
One should contemplate [the enemy] as being terrified by various cruel, fierce, and wrathfully terrible rākṣasas; by that means, even Vajradhara himself will die. 89.
Contemplating how [the body] is devoured by owls, crows, vultures, jackals, and long-beaked creatures, one realizes that even a Buddha is certainly destroyed;
it is like a black serpent, exceedingly cruel, and a source of terror even to fear itself. (90)
Having meditated upon that supreme poison-samaya on the forehead, it becomes distinguished;
once consumed by that serpent, even a Buddha will certainly perish.

This supreme exhortation is the best means for bringing about the downfall of all beings in the ten directions, whether they cause harm or distress, and it is most excellent for [the destruction of] one's enemies.
If the practitioner strikes him on the chest with a fierce mallet, even Śakra would perish from life, according to the words of the Vajra-dharma. (93)
One should contemplate the striking and the pounding by means of the vajra-axe and other weapons of the Vajrin;
even the formidable Vajrasattva, the bestower of the three bodies, dies. 94.
One should pierce the protective mantras and deities;
for this is the supreme among the supreme rites of slaying, a commitment difficult to transgress. (95)
One should contemplate that as many beings as there are within the mandala by means of the Skandhavajra have attained the nature of luminosity; they are satisfied in this way, and not otherwise. 96.
The Buddha, the Teacher Vajradhara, and even Vajradharma, the wielder of the wheel,
die through the yoga of the *vyāḍa*, just as was spoken by Cittavajra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Fierce Vajra-Krodha of the Samaya.
Then the King Vajradhara, the Great Sage who is all-pervading space.
The perfectly awakened one of all consecrations uttered the Wisdom Vajra. || 98 ||
Oh, how naturally pure is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna!
The Victors have taught that there is arising even for phenomena that are unarisen. || 99 ||

In this regard, here is the secret of the minor ritual: one should draw a deformed and terrifying serpent with chalk and charcoal—blazing with black flames, enraged, double-tongued, and garlanded with fangs. (100)
In this regard, here is the heart-mantra for inciting the fierce nāgas:
Khaṃ.
One should visualize the poison, brilliant as *hālāhala*, situated within the mouth;
herein is this heart-mantra for attracting all poisons.
Nir.
One should meditate that all poison existing within the three realms, arising from various sources, has been extracted; one should contemplate it as falling away by means of that [mantra]. 101.
At that very moment, he would become a most terrible ocean of poison;
as soon as he is touched, he would destroy the entire world—of this there is no doubt. Thus he spoke.
Frogs, scorpions, and various kinds of snakes are to be fashioned according to the prescribed ritual, characterized by the specific features of their respective sacrificial origins.
In this regard, here is the heart-mantra for the great transference of all poisons: || -85- ||
Oṃ.
Having drawn forth the wicked poisons such as vajra-poison and other dreadful toxins by means of the wheel of gnosis, one should project them into the mandala of the space-vajra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāviṣasamayavajra. In this regard, here is the Vajra-heart for the treatment of poison:
One should contemplate that great vajra within the heart as white in color, emitting clouds of rays intensely blazing and stainless like the light of the moon. (105)
Applying the practice of the four points, he remains there;
having manifested it two or three times, one should contemplate him as cutting [the victim]. (106)
"He makes the element of space, which is filled with poison, free from poison in an instant.
And so it is said:
"In this regard, here is the heart-mantra for attracting all poisons."
Aḥ.
Gonorrhea, boils, scabies, and whatever other diseases are known, perish by mere meditation, according to the word of Vajrapāṇi. (107)
One should contemplate a great eight-petaled lotus, stainless like the moon;
situated in its center, one should visualize [the deity] filled with five-colored rays of light.
One should withdraw the black phase and, during the impelling, visualize it as white;
this is the secret stage of meditation, a mystery pure with primordial wisdom.
Thus [ends the verse]. 109.
In this regard, these are the vajra-heart mantra syllables and phrases for the medical treatment of external and internal diseases:
Jinajik (Victorious over the Conquerors)
ĀROLIK.
Vajradhṛk.
Whatever syllable or word may be desired as bringing about the quality of devotion,
one should contemplate such a disease through the impelling of the universal vajra.
Alternatively, one should contemplate [the seed-syllable] emerging from the state of one's own body, speech, and mind, having the form of a monkey or arising from a dog. 111.
Having meditated upon either a wheel or a vajra while abiding in the vajra-position,
one should visualize the commitment of body, speech, and mind as being pulverized by it.
From that time forth, the perfectly awakened ones and the highly renowned bodhisattvas, with joyful eyes, bestow the delightful state of empowerment. (113)
And thus it is said:
"One should contemplate clouds of Buddhas within the vajras of one's own body and mind;
one should meditate upon the great cloud of Vajrarāga as the liberation from disease."
Thus [ends the section]. 114.
For one who meditates while enraged upon all the Buddhas of the ten directions and the wise Vajrasattvas, their ultimate slaying occurs. 115.
By this mere meditation, whatever is known to arise from karma is destroyed within seven days through the application of one hundred and eight recitations.
Alternatively, the procedure for vajra-meditation is taught by means of one’s own king of mantras;
for this is the samaya regarding all diseases, which is difficult to transgress. (117)
Then King Vajradhara, of great splendor with the hook of gnosis, the great vajra of desire and liberation, spoke these words: || 118 ||
Regarding phenomena that are like dreams, whose intrinsic nature is non-arising, and whose reality is pure by nature, the Vajra of Delusion is proclaimed. (119)
Practitioners who are constantly devoted to recitation and meditation behold Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in two distinct ways. (120)
In this regard, here is the section on the commitment of the great dream:
One sees the supreme attainment of the wisdom of awakening, which is brilliantly radiant;
or one quickly perceives oneself as the Buddha’s enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya). || 121 ||
He sees him being honored by the great beings of the three realms,
as well as by the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, and even by the five strands of sensual pleasure.
He beholds the worshiped image, possessing a radiance equal to great primordial wisdom. || 122 ||
The one of great renown, the Great Secret Vajra, beholds in a dream the great form of Vajrasattva, the great-minded Vajradharma, as his own self-form. 123.
The great Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajra-holders pay homage;
such a dream will be seen, which bestows the accomplishments of body, speech, and mind. (124)
Seeing a beautiful celestial maiden adorned with all ornaments, or a boy or a girl, he attains accomplishment.
One certainly beholds all the Buddhas of the ten directions abiding in their fields;
with a joyful mind, they bestow the delightful treasury of Dharma. (126)
Established in the vajra of meditative concentration, one beholds at the time of yoga the body situated within the wheel of Dharma, surrounded by all the Buddhas. 127.
During the time of meditative concentration, he beholds various pleasure groves adorned with celestial maidens and others, all sustained by the empowerment of all the Buddhas.
He sees himself consecrated by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
he sees himself being honored by the great kings of the Vidyādharas. || 129 ||
And so he said:
He sees various stainless dreams born of the vajra;
for him, the unsurpassed [attainment] born of the vajra of body, speech, and mind is accomplished. 130.
If one of vajra-intellect beholds outcasts, dogs, corpses, and so forth, the abode of the mind of the wise Vajrasattva is accomplished. (131)
In this regard, here is the heart of the occasion for investigating dreams:

"One's own mind is established in the contemplation of the mind; all phenomena are situated therein. For these phenomena abide in the space-vajra; they are neither phenomena nor the nature of phenomena. (132)
-88- Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, filled with wonder and struck by amazement, questioned Vajrasattva, the dispeller of all doubts regarding the body, speech, and mind of the Tathāgatas:
"O Blessed One, what is this? In phenomena that are devoid of intrinsic nature, the reality of phenomena has been proclaimed! Oh, how marvelous is this meditation on the space-like within space!"
Thus [ends the verse]. 133.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajrapāṇi of Body, Speech, and Mind, spoke thus to all the Tathāgatas:
"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, space is not conjoined with any phenomenon, nor is it unconjoined; yet it does not occur to space itself [to think]:
'This is omnipresent and it perceives everywhere.'"
In this very way, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, all phenomena, and dreams should be understood as having arisen from the dream-samaya.
Just as, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, space is indefinable, invisible, and inexpressible;
even so, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, all phenomena should be understood.
Venerable Tathāgatas, it is just as follows: the vajra-word samaya of the body, speech, and mind of all phenomena is omnipresent and of a single nature, namely, the nature of the mind.
And that which is the element of body, speech, and mind, and the element of space—these are non-dual and indivisible.
Venerable Tathāgatas, it is just as follows: all phenomena abide within the element of space.
And that space-element does not abide in the desire realm, nor does it abide in the form realm, nor does it abide in the formless realm.

That which is the dharma-realm does not abide within the three realms; for that which has no arising, there is no birth, and that which has no birth cannot be conceived by means of any phenomenon whatsoever.
Therefore, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature.
Just as, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) is that which brings about the vajra-word for the arising of the gnosis of all Tathāgatas;
and yet that thought of awakening does not abide in the body, does not abide in speech, and does not abide in the mind.
That dharma which does not abide within the triple world has no arising.
This is the vajra-word for generating the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, it does not occur to a dream: "I shall manifest the state of dreaming within the triple world."
And it does not occur to a person, "May I see a dream.
Furthermore, that activity of the three realms is like a dream, similar to a dream, and produced from a dream.

In the same way, O Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas—however many Buddhas and Bodhisattvas there are in all the world-systems of the ten directions—as well as all sentient beings, they are all to be understood through the principle of the selflessness of dreams.
–89– Venerable Tathāgatas, it is just as, for example, the wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇiratna*), which is the foremost of all jewels and endowed with all virtues.
Whatever beings may desire—be it gold, a jewel, or silver—they accomplish all of that by mere thought alone.
Yet that jewel and the rest do not abide in the mind, nor do they abide in the wish-fulfilling gem.
In this very way, Blessed Ones, all *tathāgatas*, all phenomena (*dharmas*) are to be understood.
Then, the Blessed Ones, all *tathāgatas*, their eyes wide with joy, spoke thus to the *tathāgata* Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all *tathāgatas*:
"It is marvelous, Blessed One, that while all phenomena converge within the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), the qualities of a Buddha (*buddhadharma*) likewise reach convergence therein."
Then all those Blessed Buddhas and Bodhisattvas prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Vajrapāṇi and spoke thus:
"Blessed One, regarding that compendium of all mantra-vajra accomplishments which has been spoken by the Blessed One—wherein do those accomplishments of the compendium of all mantra-vajras abide?
